CLXXXIII. — To the bishop of Lund. — Concerning penalties to be imposed upon clerics who commit grave excesses. (10 December.) 200

CLXXXIV. — To the archbishops and bishops of Lombardy. — They are to protect and defend the church of Bergamo against its persecutors. (16 December.) 204

CLXXXV. — To bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches in whose parishes the monastery of Monte Cassino is known to possess churches or other estates. — He confirms the privilege by which the abbot and brethren of the monastery of Monte Cassino may pronounce sentence of excommunication upon invaders of the monastery’s property. (15 December.) 204

CLXXXVI. — To Master Sym., clerk of our venerable brother G., bishop of Palestrina, legate of the Apostolic See. — He confirms to him the scholastership of the Church of Mainz. (12 December.) 205

CLXXXVII. — To the abbot of Corbie. — He confirms his privileges. (12 December.) 205

CLXXXVIII. — To the same. — He grants him permission to use a ring. (12 December.) 205

CLXXXIX. — To the bishop, dean, and Master Wilotus, canon, of Poitiers. — He entrusts to them the case concerning the election of the bishop of Angoulême. (10 December.) 206

CXC. — To the archbishop of Sens. — He interprets the tenor of apostolic letters in certain cases. (18 December.) 209

CXCI. — To the archbishop, abbot of Saint Andrew, and people of Brindisi. — He sharply rebukes them because they had conspired against the count of Brienne and, after killing the castellan, had treacherously occupied the castle. 209

CXCII. — To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and noblemen—counts, barons, and citizens—established throughout Apulia and the Terra di Lavoro. — On the same matter. 211

CXCIII. — To J., former archbishop of Lyons. — He replies to several requests with which the archbishop had pressed the Apostolic See and sought its pronouncement. (22 December.) 213

CXCIV. — To the king of England. — He is to observe the agreement made with the wife of his late brother, the former king, concerning her dower, because she was nearly reduced to beggary. (4 January.) 220

CXCV. — To the … prior of Saint Mary New of Monte Piloso. — He is to appear before the pope, to hear the accounts of clergy and people. (3 January.) 221

CXCVI. — To the … bishop of Pécs. — He is to take more attentive care for his reputation. (7 January.) 221

CXCVII. — To the abbot of Pratea, the priors of Exoldun and Nundriac, in the diocese of Bourges. — They are to cause W. de Securo to be received as canon and brother by the bishop and dean of Clermont. (5 January.) 222

CXCVIII. — To the … archbishop of Lund. — He is to lead the clergy to chastity. (17 December.) 223

CXCIX. — To the same. — Concerning penance to be imposed upon a clerk falsely accused. (17 December.) 223

CC. — To the dean and chapter of Reims. — Having rejected the election of John, bishop of Beauvais, as archbishop of Reims, he commands them to proceed without delay to another election. (10 January.) 224

CCI. — To the nobleman, duke of Austria. — Confirmation of the judgment that he is not bound to contract the marriage promised by oath with the daughter of the duke of Bohemia, because the condition had not been fulfilled. (7 January.) 225

CCII. — To the archdeacon of Vicenza. — He confirms him in the archdeaconry. (3 January.) 225

CCIII. — To the … bishops of Osma, Burgos, and Zamora. — He entrusts to them the accusation brought against the bishop of Astorga. (12 January.) 227

CCIV. — To the … abbot and convent of Saint Alban. — They are to receive a certain church in order to pay the debts of its deceased possessor, a crusader. (15 January.) 228

CCV. — To Master Martin, clerk of Holy Cross of Coimbra. — He receives him under protection. (24 January.) 229

CCVI. — To the noblemen Manuel, James, Odo, Censius, and Deodatus Frangipani. — He settles the controversies between them and the people of Terracina. (19 January.) 229

CCVII. — To Gonsaldus, prior of the church of Holy Cross of Coimbra, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity. — He receives them under the protection of Saint Peter, and their possessions are enumerated. (13 January.) 232

[Col. 1621]

CCVIII. — To the chapter of Wells. — They are to receive Master Rog. Porretanus as a canon and brother. (15 January.) 233

CCIX. — To P., cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, legate of the Apostolic See. — He rejoices that he has reached Cyprus to assist the Holy Land, and leaves to his discretion whether he should communicate with the excommunicated Venetians. (23 January.) 235

CCX. — Letter of Alexius, emperor of Constantinople. — He acknowledges the Roman pontiff as head of the universal Church, and
He swears devotion. (VII Kalends of September.)

236 CCXI.—Letters of the crusaders.—The destruction of Zara, and the restoration to Emperor Alexius of the empire seized by the murderers of Isaac; he promises reverence to the Roman Church.

237 CCXII.—From the King of Hungary to the pope.—He informs him that Ban Culin had firmly bound himself that, should he thereafter presume to defend heretics in his land, he would pay one thousand marks of silver, one half to the Apostolic See and the other to the king’s treasury.

240 CCXIII.—… To the prioress of the monastery of Claret and her sisters, present and future, professing the monastic life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection. (VII Kalends of February.)

240 CCXIV.—To the Archbishop of Nidaros and his suffragans.—The pope rejoices at the death of King Sverre, who had usurped the kingdom, and at the succession of his son, who had recalled them; finally, he sharply rebukes the archbishop, who had absolved persons whom he had no power to absolve. (IX Kalends of February.)

241 CCXV.—To the … Bishop of Liège.—That he compel the Bishop of Utrecht, under penalty of excommunication and deposition, to satisfy the creditors of his church. (II Kalends of February.)

242 CCXVI.—To the Archbishop, dean, and archdeacon of Bourges.—He grants them authority to investigate the Archbishop of Bordeaux, concerning whom the most disgraceful reports were circulating. (V Kalends of February.)

243 CCXVII.—To the abbots of Tenalia and Madio, and the chanter of Saintes.—He entrusts to them the reform and ordering of the monastery of Albaterrensis. (V Kalends of February.)

245 CCXVIII.—To the same.—That they compel the Abbot of Albaterrensis to restore to B., a canon of Albaterrensis, the church of Saint James. (V Kalends of February.)

248 CCXIX.—To the Bishop of Alatri.—Concerning the annulment of an oath unlawfully extorted for satisfaction of an injury. (III Nones of February.)

249 CCXX.—To the … Bishop of Maturana; the … abbots of Coratio and of Saint Mary of Aquaformosa; and the treasurer of Marturana.—That they investigate the exchange of the church of Botrano between the abbot and convent of Flora on the one hand and the Archbishop and church of Cosenza on the other. (VIII Ides of February.)

250 CCXXI.—To the Archbishop and canons of Embrun.—That they receive Master P., the pope’s scribe, as a canon and brother. (IV Nones of February.)

252 CCXXII.—To the Archbishop of Cosenza.—That he not alter the ancient customs of his church. (Nones of February.)

254 CCXXIII.—To the dean and chapter of Évreux.—He grants that anything obtained in apostolic letters against their rights shall be deemed void. (VIII Ides of February.)

254 CCXXIV.—To the same.—A similar indulgence. (VIII Ides of February.)

255 CCXXV.—To the Abbot of Persenia, H., archdeacon, and S. of Bairo, canon of Chartres.—That they see to the abolition of an evil custom concerning parish churches in the diocese of Évreux. (VIII Ides of February.)

255 CCXXVI.—To the abbots of Alneto, Ardena, and Fontaneto.—He orders them to absolve the abbot and convent of Saint-Ouen of Rouen from promises of benefices made contrary to the decrees of the Lateran Council. (II Nones of February.)

256 CCXXVII.—To the … Bishop of Geneva.—He annuls judgments rendered in the case between him and the Abbot of Siz. (VII Ides of February.)

257 CCXXVIII.—To Michael, subdeacon.—He confirms by apostolic authority his possession of the benefice in the church of Castries granted him by the Bishop of Maguelonne. (VII Ides of February.)

258 CCXXIX.—To Alexius, Emperor of Constantinople.—A letter in reply.

259 CCXXX.—To the noblemen B., Marquis of Montferrat; B. of Flanders; L. of Blois; H. of Saint-Pol, counts; and the other crusader barons: the spirit of sounder counsel.—Concerning the promise of the Emperor of Constantinople, [Col. 1622] and that he ought to swear obedience and reverence to the Roman Church, and that the patriarch ought to receive the pallium from the body of Saint Peter.

260 CCXXXI.—To the Bishops of Soissons and Troyes.—On the same subject.

261 CCXXXII.—To the same.—That they lead the crusaders to repentance.

262 CCXXXIII.—To the Abbot and convent of Albamarla.—A privilege.

263 CCXXXIV.—To the convent of Saint Euphemia.—That they receive John, chaplain of the pope, as abbot. (Nones of February.)

264 CCXXXV.—To the … illustrious King of Aragon.—He postpones the legation to Spain to another time. (XVI Kalends of March.)

265 CCXXXVI.—To the Archbishop of Sens.—He gives his reasons for having previously written too harshly and consoles him. (XVI Kalends of March.)

266 CCXXXVII.—To the monks of the monastery of Molesme.—That they not borrow money without the consent of the abbot and convent. (XI Kalends of March.)

269 CCXXXVIII.—To the dean and chapter of Évreux.—That no layman possessing a right of patronage in churches may exact tithes. (VII Ides of February.)

269 CCXXXIX.—To the Bishop of Auxerre.—That he rise up to extirpate heretical depravity. (XI Kalends of March.)

269 CCXL.—To the Archbishop-elect of Grado.—He reproves him for delaying the office of consecration and threatens him. (X Kalends of March.)

270 CCXLI.—To the Abbots of Saint-Èvre and Saint Leo, and Master R., archdeacon of Toul.—That a legate of the Apostolic See may confer benefices even without consulting the patrons. (X Kalends of March.)

271 CCXLII.—To the Bishop of Agde and the Abbot of Saint-Pons.—He confirms by apostolic authority the sentence of suspension pronounced against the Bishop of Béziers by P. of Castelnau and Radulph, monks of Fontfroide and legates of the Apostolic See. (XII Kalends of March.)

272 CCXLIII.—To the Archbishop of Narbonne.—A lamentable letter: his whole province is full of heretics. (IV Kalends of February.)

273 CCXLIV.—To Master Robert.—He explains the decretal letter *Licet Heli*.

275 CCXLV.—To the Abbot of Cancellata; Master B., canon of Albeterrensis, of the diocese of Périgueux; and A. de La Faia, canon of Saint-Front of Périgueux.—That they ensure that J. Morelli, clerk, nominated as canon and brother in the Church of Angoulême, enjoys the prebend. (VII Ides of February.)

276 BOOK SEVEN.—Seventh year of the pontificate, A.D. 1204.

277 I.—To Calojohn, King of the Bulgarians and Vlachs, and his successors.—A privilege by which Leo, priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross and legate of the Apostolic See, is granted authority to anoint and crown him king. (VI Kalends of March.)

280 II.—To the Archbishop of Trnovo.—He likewise establishes the Archbishop of Trnovo as primate of all Bulgaria and Vlachia, and sends him such a privilege through the said legate.

282 III.—To B., Archbishop of Trnovo and primate of the Bulgarians and Vlachs.—He informs him that he has caused the Bishop of Brandizuberensis to be anointed. He orders that henceforth both the primate and the metropolitan bishops and priests of his province receive anointing, etc.

287 IV.—Instrument by which the King of Bulgaria and Vlachia subjects his empire to the Roman Church.

288 V.—Letter of Basil, Archbishop of Trnovo.—He writes that, when he wished to proceed to the Apostolic See, his passage was blocked at Dyrrachium; then, recalled by the emperor, he was invested with the pallium in September, on the feast of the Nativity.

290 VI.—Letter of Calojohn to Pope Innocent.—On the same subject as the preceding letter.

292 VII.—To Anastasius, Archbishop of Belesbudes.—He sends him the pallium.

292 VIII.—To the illustrious King of the Bulgarians and Vlachs.—He informs him that he has ordered the legate to anoint him and grant him the royal insignia.

292 IX.—To the Archbishop of Trnovo, primate of all Bulgaria and Vlachia, and the other archbishops, bishops, clergy, and people established in Bulgaria and Vlachia.—He sends him the pallium.

294 X.—Form by which the pallium is to be delivered to the Archbishops of Belesbudes and Trnovo.

294 XI.—Form of the oath taken by the Archbishop of Trnovo.

[Col. 1623] XII.—To Calojohn, illustrious King of the Bulgarians and Vlachs.—He sends him a banner.

295 XIII.—To archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches, and to all clergy and laity established in the kingdom of Hungary.—He writes to them concerning the restoration of the Bulgarians and that they should treat the legate well.

296 XIV.—To archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches, and to all the clergy established in the province of Serbia.—On the same subject.

297 XV.—To the Bishop of Ely and the … Abbot of Saint Edmund’s.—That they ensure satisfaction is made to Roman merchants concerning money owed them by Roger of Saint Edmund’s. (VI Nones of May.)

298 XVI.—To the prior and brothers of the Hospital of Thuregano.—He receives them under protection, with an annual payment of one gold piece. (III Ides of May.)

300 XVII.—To the Bishop of Oloron and the Abbots of Plana Silva and Saint-Sever.—That they appoint a coadjutor to the Archbishop of Auch, who suffers from epilepsy. (III Ides of March.)

300 XVIII.—To the nobleman, … Doge of the Venetians: the spirit of sounder counsel.—He exhorts him and the Venetians to come to their senses and do penance for the crime they committed against Zara. (VI Kalends of March.)

301 XIX.—To the prioress and nuns of Ruesperra.—He receives them under protection. (II Nones of March.)

302 XX.—To the Bishop of Fiesole.—That he not obey the Florentine consuls, who had arranged to transfer the said bishopric to the city of Florence, alleging a right of patronage; he orders this claim to be quashed. (III Ides of March.)

303 XXI.—To the Prior of Saint Fridianus of Lucca.—On the same subject. (Ides of March.)

304 XXII.—To the archpriest and G. and R., master-canons of Lucca.—In favor of Noradus, subdeacon: that they not allow him to be harassed by vexatious proceedings. (XIV Kalends of April.)

305 XXIII.—To the consuls and people of Camerino.—That they recover and preserve the possessions of the Roman Church in the castle of Camerino. (VIII Kalends of April.)

305 XXIV.—To the Bishop and chapter of Luni.—He confirms by apostolic authority the transfer of the bishopric of Luni to Sarzana. (VIII Kalends of April.)

306 XXV.—To the Abbot of Saint Stephen and Master Lanfranc, canon of Bologna.—Concerning the revocation of a sentence in an unspecified case. (XV Kalends of April.)

307 XXVI.—To N.—That an inquiry be made concerning suspicious privileges and indulgences. (III Kalends of April.)

307 XXVII.—To the Prior of Saint Stephen of Fano.—By apostolic authority he decides the case between him and M., Bishop of Fano, concerning the church of Saint Stephen. (V Kalends of March.)

308 XXVIII.—To R. de Geclewerds, G. de Driburg, and Master T., rector of the church of Lilleschae.—He entrusts to them for judgment the case between the abbot and monks of Melrose and the nobleman Albanus. (II Nones of March.)

309 XXIX.—To the … Archbishop of Canterbury.—He replies to him concerning appeals. (VI Kalends of April.)

311 XXX.—To the dean and canons of Holy Cross of Stampis.—He receives them under protection. (VI Kalends of April.)

312 XXXI.—To the Archbishop and dean of Rouen.—That they may render the required justice to the brothers of the Hospital of Jerusalem. (X Kalends of April.)

313 XXXII.—To the … Abbot of Corona, the … Archdeacon of Saint-Brieuc, and the subdean of Saint Peter of Poitiers.—That, upon going to the monastery of Saint Hilary of Cella, they reform it. (Kalends of March.)

314 XXXIII.—To J., prior, and the brothers of the church of Saint Stephen of Fano.—He receives them under protection. (XIII Kalends of April.)

315 XXXIV.—To the … Archbishop of Canterbury, the Bishop of Ely, and the … Abbot of Saint Edmund’s.—He confirms the judgment rendered in the case of the church of Filebi. (XVI Kalends of April.)

316 XXXV.—To the … Bishop of Ely, the … Abbot of Saint Edmund’s, and the … Dean of Cîteaux.—That they investigate privileges granted to the chapter of York. (Kalends of April.)

316 XXXVI.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, counts, barons, and all clergy and people established in Sicily and Calabria.—He sends to them G., cardinal-deacon of the title of Saint Adrian, legate of the Apostolic See, and commends him to them. (Kalends of April.)

317 XXXVII.—To the Abbot and monks of Saint Julian, the Hospitallers of the Cross, and other clerics of the diocese of Rimini.—That they observe the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the Bishop of Rimini against heretics. (Nones of April.)

319 XXXVIII.—To the Archbishop of Siponto.—Concerning a woman who, her husband being impotent, took another man; after the first man’s death, the second refused her, although he had [Col. 1624] offspring by her: the pope orders that this cannot be done. (Kalends of April.)

320 XXXIX.—To Ventura, Bishop of Rimini, and his canonically appointed successors, in perpetuity.—He receives him under protection and confirms the possessions of his church. (VI Ides of April.)

321 XL.—To the Abbot and convent of Casa Dei.—Concerning restoration of the bishopric in the church of Montepiloso.

321 XLI.—To the … Archbishop of Ravenna.—That he restrain the podestà and consuls of Modena who were violating ecclesiastical liberty in the city of Modena. (II Ides of April.)

323 XLII.—To the archbishops and bishops established throughout France.—On the same subject as letters 164, 165, and 166 of Book VI.

325 XLIII.—To Peter de Maliano, rector of the hospital of Pulchicavellis. (Nones of April.)

328 XLIV.—To the Abbot of Casamari.—Commission for hearing the case between the Kings of France and England.

329 XLV.—To the … Archbishops of Cologne, Trier, and Sens, the chapter of Reims, and their suffragans.—That they ensure observance of the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the Bishop of Cambrai against the Count of Namur and others. (IV Ides of April.)

330 XLVI.—To Master Thomas de Disce, canon of Vuellensis.—He confirms by apostolic authority the prebend conferred on him by the Archbishop of York.

332 XLVII.—To the … Bishop of Wadara and the … Abbot of Petis, in the diocese of Veszprém.—That they investigate whether a bishopric ought to be established in certain Greek churches in the kingdom of Hungary. (XVI Kalends of May.)

332 XLVIII.—To the Abbot of Saint-Aubert, S., archdeacon, and Master Ren., canon, of Cambrai.—On the same subject as letter 45. (VII Ides of May.)

333 XLIX.—To the illustrious King of Bohemia.—He is granted permission to be styled king in letters. (XIII Kalends of May.)

333 L.—To the archpriest and clerics of the people of Arezzo.—He settles the disputes between them and the provost and canons of Arezzo. (XIII Kalends of May.)

334 LI.—To the Archbishop of Mainz.—Against the citizens of Mainz, and concerning the establishment of a metropolitan see in Bohemia. (XII Kalends of May.)

336 LII.—To the illustrious King of Bohemia.—He postpones his petition for the erection of a metropolitan see in Bohemia and orders him to obtain the consent of the Archbishop of Mainz. (XI Kalends of May.)

337 LIII.—To the canons and ministeriales of Mainz: the spirit of sounder counsel.—Much concerning their rebellion against the Church and the archbishop. (XI Kalends of May.)

338 LIV.—To the illustrious King of Bohemia.—He confirms by apostolic authority the privileges granted him by emperors and recently confirmed by Otto. (XVII Kalends of May.)

339 LV.—To the … Bishops of Prague and Olomouc and the … Archdeacon of Behin.—That, if anyone attempts to inflict any harm upon the King of Bohemia, they restrain him with ecclesiastical censures. (XI Kalends of May.)

339 LVI.—To the Archbishop of Esztergom.—Concerning the transfer of a certain provostship. (VIII Kalends of May.)

340 LVII.—To the same.—That he crown the son of the King of Hungary, since the king had resolved to go to the Holy Land. (VIII Kalends of May.)

340 LVIII.—To the illustrious King of Hungary.—He explains the command already issued concerning the provostships of the kingdom of Hungary. (VIII Kalends of May.)

340 LIX.—To Hugh, Abbot of the monastery of Saint Augustine of Monte-Alto, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (IV Kalends of May.)

341 LX.—To the … Bishops of Lincoln and Worcester.—In favor of a certain canon: that they not permit him to be harassed by the Archbishop of York. (V Ides of May.)

342 LXI.—To the dean and chapter of the duke’s chapel at Dijon.—That they may not be excommunicated by anyone except in two cases. (VI Ides of May.)

343 LXII.—To the … Archdeacon, the … Archpriest, and the whole chapter of the Gargano church.—He confirms the ancient customs of their church. (VI Ides of May.)

343 LXIII.—To the master and brothers of the Hospital of Bekekeg.—He receives them under protection. (XII Kalends of June.)

344 LXIV.—To the … Bishop of Mantua.—That he receive, in the pope’s name, the lands of Countess Matilda situated in his diocese. (II Ides of May.)

344 LXV.—To the … Abbot and convent of Silvamajor.—He receives them under protection. (XI Kalends of June.)

344 LXVI.—To the Abbot of Afflighem, Master R., parson of the church of Tenis, and Gilbert, canon of Utrecht.—That they [Col. 1625] investigate W., dean of Utrecht, who had passed from the regular life to the secular. (Ides of May.)

344 LXVII.—To the … Archbishop of Toledo and the … Bishops of Burgos and Zamora.—He commands them to absolve B., daughter of the King of Castile, who had left the King of León and sought the benefit of absolution. (XI Kalends of June.)

345 LXVIII.—To the … Bishop, dean, and … precentor of Hereford.—That they investigate the case of John, master of the hospital of York. (II Ides of May.)

346 LXIX.—To the same.—On the same subject. (XIII Kalends of June.)

347 LXX.—To the provost and canons of Saint Gereon at Cologne.—That they confirm, in accordance with the apostolic mandate, a prebend for Ricc., the pope’s scribe. (V Nones of May.)

348 LXXI.—To the … Abbot of Werden in the diocese of Cologne; the … provost of Runnensis (192); and the … provost of Saint Cunibert at Cologne.—He entrusts to them the examination of the election of the Bishop of Münster. (V Kalends of June.)

350 LXXII.—To the … Bishop of Zamora.—Concerning a case of a boy seeking promotion to holy orders although he had been implicated in the death of a person. (XII Kalends of June.)

353 LXXIII.—To the chapter of Saint Cecilia.—He confirms by apostolic authority the judgment rendered in their favor in the case between them and the archpriest of the church of Saint Lawrence at Pozzuoli. (VI Kalends of June.)

353 LXXIV.—To the … Archbishop-elect of Grado.—A threatening letter because he had delayed consecration and petitioning for the pallium, and because of the Venetians’ offense. (Kalends of June.)

354 LXXV.—To the … Abbot of Cîteaux and P. and R., monks of Fontfroide, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they investigate charges against the Archbishop of Narbonne, notorious for numerous vices and accusations. (V Kalends of June.)

355 LXXVI.—To the Abbot of Cîteaux and the monks of Fontfroide, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they proceed against heretics. (II Kalends of June.)

358 LXXVII.—Written to the … Archbishops of Aix, Arles, and Narbonne, their suffragans, and the abbots, priors, deans, archdeacons, and other prelates of churches established in their provinces.—On the same subject as the preceding letter.

360 LXXVIII.—To the Archbishop of Narbonne.—He deprives him of the abbey of Montearagón, which had previously been entrusted to him, because the offices are incompatible. (IV Kalends of June.)

360 LXXIX.—To the King of France.—That he assist the apostolic legates against heretics. (V Kalends of June.)

361 LXXX.—To Peter of Paris, chaplain above Lincoln Bridge.—He receives him under the protection of Saint Peter, with an annual payment of one bezant. (Kalends of June.)

362 LXXXI.—To the canons of Cosenza.—That they give consent to the exchange of the church of Rotrano. (II Nones of June.)

363 LXXXII.—To the citizens of Cosenza.—On the same subject. (II Nones of June.)

365 LXXXIII.—To the podestà and people of Assisi.—Concerning their oath to abide by the commands of the Apostolic See, and many other matters. (VIII Ides of June.)

365 LXXXIV.—To the … Archbishop of Embrun and the beloved son, the … Abbot of Boscaudun.—That they diligently investigate the offenses of the Bishop of Vence. (VI Ides of June.)

366 LXXXV.—To the Prior of Essebi, Master H. de Gillevillis, canon of Lincoln, and Master A. de Wilna, rector of the church of Bareswuh in the diocese of Lincoln.—That proceedings be taken in the case of Agnes, a woman whom her father and stepmother had forced unwillingly into a monastery. (II Kalends of June.)

368 LXXXVI.—To the prior and monks of Saint Andrew of Arce.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (VII Kalends of June.)

368 LXXXVII.—To the … Prior and monks of Folkestone.—On a similar subject. (VII Kalends of June.)

369 LXXXVIII.—To the … Prior and monks of the monastery of Saint Andrew of Stokes.—On a similar subject. (III Ides of June.)

370 LXXXIX.—To the … Abbot of Salem.—Concerning the absolution of the Bishop of Constance. (XVII [incomplete].)

370 XC.—To the Bishop and archdeacon of Pavia.—Concerning the conferral of certain prebends in the Church of Asti. (XVII Kalends of July.)

371 XCI.—To the … Abbot and convent of Casa Dei.—He assigns a peremptory deadline for responding concerning the affair of Montepiloso. (XV Kalends of July.)

373 XCII.—To the … Archbishop and the … provost of Saint Mary of Albario, Genoese.—That they restrain S., mother-in-law of N. de Camilla, who was challenging her son-in-law’s marriage. (XVII Kalends of July.)

373 XCIII.—To the … Archbishops of Compostela and Toledo, and the … Bishops of Tarazona and Coimbra.—That they [Col. 1626] induce the daughter of the King of Castile to restore to the King of León the towns which he had assigned to her, whether as dowry or as a gift on account of marriage. (XII Kalends of July.)

374 XCIV.—To the … Archbishop of Compostela and the … Bishops of Zamora and Palencia.—That they absolve the repentant King of León. (XIII Kalends of July.)

376 XCV.—To Guido, master of the Hospital of Saint Mary in Saxia, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He unites the Hospital of Saint Mary in Saxia with the Hospital of the Holy Spirit at Montpellier, for the salvation of the Roman pontiff and the cardinals; with many privileges. (XIV Kalends of July.)

376 XCVI.—To the … Bishop and the … provost of Uzès.—He annuls letters of confirmation obtained concerning the administration of certain canons of Nîmes. (XVII Kalends of July.)

380 XCVII.—To the … Bishop and chapter of Laon.—That they admit to a priestly prebend the person whom Hubald, subdeacon and canon of the Church of Laon, may nominate at the time of vacancy, by reason of authority granted him by the bishop. (X Kalends of July.)

381 XCVIII.—To the chapter of Vicenza.—By apostolic authority he confers the provostship of Vicenza upon Nicholas, his subdeacon. (VIII Kalends of July.)

382 XCIX.—To the Bishop of Passau.—He grants him the freedom, since he had been elected Patriarch of Aquileia, to remain at his own discretion either in that metropolitan see or in the see of Passau. (VI Ides of June.)

383 C.—To J., Bishop of Furcone.—He confirms by apostolic authority the donation to the Bishop of Furcone of the hamlet of Saint Gusanius [otherwise Eusanius], made by Roger, King of Sicily. The instrument of donation is inserted. (XVII Kalends of July.)

385 CI.—To the Bishops of Avignon, Tricastin, and … Cavaillon.—That they ensure the firm observance of the sentence of interdict pronounced against the provost and canons of Sisteron in the case between them and the brethren of the Knights Templar concerning a certain oratory. (XI Kalends of July.)

386 CII.—To the nobleman John Oddonis, our kinsman.—On the advice of the city judges, he grants him lordship over Montorio and another castle called Caminaras. The judges’ opinion is inserted. (VIII Kalends of June.)

387 CIII.—To the noblewoman … daughter of the late Judge of Gallura.—That she abide by the counsel of the Archbishop of Torres concerning contracting marriage. (VI Nones of July.)

389 CIV.—To the Archbishop of Cagliari.—On the same subject. (VI Nones of July.)

389 CV.—To the bishops and noblemen, freemen in the judicature of Gallura.—On the same subject.

390 CVI.—To the nobleman … Judge of Cagliari.—On the same subject. (V Nones of July.)

390 CVII.—To the Archbishop of Torres.—Since the Judge of Torres and his wife were related in the fourth and fifth degrees of consanguinity, and grave scandal would otherwise arise from a divorce, he entrusts the case to the prelate’s judgment. (VI Nones of July.)

390 CVIII.—To the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches established throughout Sardinia.—He orders them to furnish the Archbishop of Torres, who labors for the Roman pontiff, with necessities for his maintenance. (V Nones of July.)

391 CIX.—To the Archbishop of Pisa.—That the Marquis of Cagliari swear fealty to the Roman Church, since Sardinia belongs by right and property to that Church. (V Nones of July.)

391 CX.—To the Archbishop of Torres.—That he ought not defer to the Archbishop of Pisa unless the latter is in the province of Torres, although he has received from the Apostolic See privileges of legation and primacy in Sardinia. (V Nones of July.)

392 CXI.—To the prelates of exempt churches established in Sardinia.—He rebukes them because they have recourse to a secular tribunal. (V Nones of July.)

392 CXII.—To the Archbishop of Torres.—He grants him authority to correct delinquent and dissolute clerics. (V Nones of July.)

393 CXIII.—To the nobleman … Judge of Torres.—That he not interfere in clerics’ lawsuits or impede ecclesiastical liberty. (V Nones of July.)

394 CXIV.—To the Bishop of Hildesheim and the Provost of Magdeburg.—Concerning the absolution of the Bishop-elect of Merseburg. (Kalends of July.)

395 CXV.—To J., Bishop of Furcone, and his canonically appointed successors, in perpetuity.—He receives him under protection, and the possessions belonging to his church are enumerated. (Kalends of July.)

396 CXVI.—To the chapter of Reims.—He raises many objections concerning the election of an archbishop; and, provided that he himself consents, he has provided G., Cardinal-Bishop of Palestrina, as archbishop. (II Nones of July.)

398 CXVII.—To N.—He entrusts to him the case concerning the deanship of the Church of Clermont, between G. de Cros, Archdeacon [Col. 1627] of Clermont, on the one side, and the chapter of Clermont and Parentius, subdeacon of the pope, on the other. (IV Ides of July.)

402 CXVIII.—To N.—That they induce the prior and monks of Durham to render the bishop due obedience. (XIV Kalends of July.)

405 CXIX.—To Assalitus, canon.—Dispensation for defect of birth. (III Kalends of August.)

405 CXX.—To N.—On the same subject. (VII Kalends of August.)

406 CXXI.—To N.—Concerning the ordination by Greek bishops of priests, both Greek and Latin. (IV Nones of August.)

407 CXXII.—To N., N.—He confirms by apostolic authority the judgment by which a tithe conferred upon G., deacon, by the Bishop of Amiens was adjudged to him against J. de Canduetre of the diocese of Noyon, who had unjustly occupied that same tithe; and he orders them to protect the said G. from all molestation and ensure restoration to him of what had been taken. (VI Kalends of August.)

407 CXXIII.—To N.—He assigns to Robert, deacon of Vezelay, who lacks every ecclesiastical benefice, the first prebend to fall vacant in the Church of Soissons. (XVII Kalends of September.)

408 CXXIV.—To NN.—That they ensure the reception, without violence, of Rog. de Bisatiis as rector by the citizens of Besançon. (Kalends of September.)

409 CXXV.—To NN.—On the same subject as letter 124. (Kalends of September.)

410 CXXVI.—To H., King of Hungary.—He is deeply grieved that, on Hungary’s borders, he had wrongfully impeded the legate cardinal’s passage to Bulgaria; he admonishes him to correct this error, lest he be compelled to take action against him.

410 CXXVII.—To L., priest-cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross, legate of the Apostolic See.—He responds to the King of Hungary’s complaints. (XVII Kalends of October.)

413 CXXVIII.—To the illustrious King of Hungary.—Concerning the election of the Abbot of Saint Giles of Hungary. (XVIII Kalends of October.)

417 CXXIX.—To the … illustrious King of Sicily.—He sends G., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Adrian, to conduct such negotiations as must be conducted with the king and to establish peace. (IV Nones of October.)

419 CXXX.—To the nobleman W. Caparoni: the spirit of sounder counsel.—On the same subject as the preceding letter. (IV Nones of October.)

419 CXXXI.—To L., royal protonotary.—On a similar subject. (IV Nones of October.)

420 CXXXII.—To the … Bishop of Limoges.—That they cause Master W. Brunater to be received as a canon in the Church of Angoulême. (Nones of October.)

421 CXXXIII.—To the nobleman Richard, our kinsman.—He confirms various possessions to him. (VII Ides of October.)

422 CXXXIV.—To archbishops and bishops established throughout France.—He declares them exempt from the sentence of interdict pronounced by the Abbot of … Casamari in the affair of peace between the Kings of England and France. (Lateran, VII Ides of August.)

425 CXXXV.—To G., Cardinal-Deacon of Saint Adrian, legate of the Apostolic See.—On the same subject as letter 129 of this seventh book. (IV Nones of October.)

425 CXXXVI.—To P., Bishop-elect of Palermo.—He exhorts him to make peace. (III Nones of October.)

426 CXXXVII.—To the … illustrious King of Hungary.—He congratulates him on having allowed passage to the legate and exhorts him to treat him kindly and honorably.

427 CXXXVIII.—To the Archdeacon of Pavia.—That he may proceed in the case entrusted to him between William de Tabiaco and the Abbot of Clavat in the diocese of Milan. (Nones of October.)

427 CXXXIX.—To the … Archbishop of Bremen and his suffragans, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established in the province of Bremen.—That he invite the faithful to take the cross against the barbarians of Livonia. (VI Ides of October.)

428 CXL.—To the … Archbishop of Torres.—That he cause Ytochor de Thorum, who had killed an acolyte unknown to him, to be absolved. (III Ides of October.)

430 CXLI.—To the same.—That he not be bound to pay debts not proved to have been converted to the uses of the church. (II Ides of October.)

430 CXLII.—To Popo, Bishop-elect of Passau.—He confirms to him the parishes of Saint Agatha and Stadeloit, assigned to the episcopal mensa. (Ides of October.)

431 CXLIII.—To the same.—He confirms to him the right of patronage of the church of Saint Mary of Passau. (Ides of October.)

431 CXLIV.—To Charles, canon of Aquileia.—He receives him under protection. (Ides of October.)

431 [Col. 1628] CXLV.—To Herluin, Bishop of Lethglennensis, and his canonically appointed successors, in perpetuity.—He receives him under protection. (Ides of October.)

432 CXLVI.—To John, priest and rector, and the brothers of the Hospital of Rivicenerarii [otherwise Riviceneratii].—He receives them under protection, subject to an annual payment. (III Kalends of November.)

433 CXLVII.—To the … podestà and people of Genoa.—That they compel the plunderers of gifts sent by Baldwin to restore the plunder. (II Nones of November.)

433 CXLVIII.—To Matthew and the brothers of the monastery of Saint Mary of Botrano.—He confirms by apostolic authority the exchange of the places of Flora and Botrano made between them on the one side and the Archbishop and chapter of Cosenza on the other. The instrument of exchange itself is inserted. (III Kalends of November.)

434 CXLIX.—To Matthew, Abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Botrano, and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (III Nones of November.)

439 CL.—To the clerics of Saint Peter at Maguelonne.—He replies that whenever the vigil falls on a Sunday, they are to fast on Saturday, and that on the day before the feast of Saint Matthias they are to observe the discipline of a fast day. (Nones of November.)

442 CLI.—To the … Bishop of Termoli and the … Abbot of Saint John in Lamis.—He entrusts to them the examination of the complaints of the people of Foggia against the people of Troia and the Bishop of Troia. (IV Kalends of October.)

442 CLII.—… Letter of Emperor Baldwin to the pope.—He informs him how the empire of Constantinople was occupied by the Latins.

447 CLIII.—To Baldwin, illustrious Emperor of Constantinople.—He replies to the preceding letter. (VII Ides of November.)

454 CLIV.—To the bishops, abbots, and other clergy in the army of crusaders at Constantinople.—He congratulates them that the empire has passed from the Greeks to the Latins and discusses the Greeks’ error concerning the faith. (Ides of November.)

455 CLV.—To the Archbishop of Lund.—That he collect the revenues of the Roman Church throughout the kingdoms of Denmark and Sweden. (Ides of November.)

461 CLVI.—To the same.—That he absolve from anathema, under specified conditions, a bailiff who had cut off the nose and injured the tongue of a priest found committing a disgraceful act with his wife. (Ides of November.)

461 CLVII.—To the same.—Authority to reform the Churches of Lund and Uppsala. (XIII Kalends of December.)

462 CLVIII.—To the same.—He sends him a pallium to deliver to the Archbishop of Uppsala in place of one lost in a fire. (XII Kalends of December.)

462 CLIX.—To the chapter of Esztergom.—He summons them to appear before him, so that they may hear judgment concerning the postulation of the Archbishop of Kalocsa as Archbishop of Esztergom. (X Kalends of December.)

463 CLX.—To M., Prior of Saint Mary Magdalene of Vallefares.—He grants him a church built by Pope Alexander and left under the ownership of Saint Peter, subject to an annual payment of two pounds of wax. (VIII Kalends of December.)

465 CLXI.—To the … Bishop and chapter of Novara.—He annuls the grant of a certain prebend made by the Archbishop of Milan. (IX Kalends of December.)

465 CLXII.—To W.

To the abbot of the monastery of Montmajour and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (3 December.) 466

CLXIII.—To the bishop of Parma.—By apostolic authority he confirms the agreement concluded between the abbot of Saint Sixtus and the commune of Cremona. (The instrument of agreement itself is inserted.) (6 December.) 470

CLXIV.—To the bishops and abbots stationed with the Christian army at Constantinople.—That Latin priests be established in the Greek Church, and that they cause a rector to be elected. (At Saint Peter’s, 7 December.) 471

CLXV.—To P. of Castronovo and Rudolf, monks of Fontfroide, legates of the Apostolic See.—He declares that, provision for benefices having been omitted, it has devolved upon the pope. (6 December.) 472

CLXVI.—To the archbishop of Arles.—That he associate with the bishop of Orange, suffering from a grave and incurable illness, a companion and coadjutor. (2 December.) 474

CLXVII.—To all who shall inspect these letters.—That the abbesses of the City may not presume, without consulting the pope or his vicar, to sell, alienate, or grant in fief immovable property. (7 December.) 475

CLXVIII.—To the archbishop of Canterbury and the bishops of Ely and Worcester.—Commission concerning restoration of a dowry, to be made by the king of England to the wife of his deceased brother, the king. (16 December.) 476

CLXIX.—To the bishop of Ely.—He replies to various questions submitted by him. (19 December.) 478

CLXX.—To the bishop of Le Puy.—That he inquire into the conduct of P., a cantor, with a certain woman. (16 December.) 484

CLXXI.—To the king of England.—That he restore the archbishop of Dublin to favour and return everything taken from him, under threat of an interdict wherever he may remain. (13 December.) 484

CLXXII.—To the dean and chapter of Noyon.—He commands that they do not delay in restoring in their entirety the prebends of the canons Renelm and Robert. (1 December.) 486

CLXXIII.—To the archbishop of Milan and his suffragans.—That they cause the people of Piacenza to be shunned as excommunicates. (16 December.) 487

CLXXIV.—To abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established throughout Lombardy.—That they assist the exiled bishop of Piacenza from the revenue owed to the Apostolic See. (18 December.) 488

CLXXV.—To the bishop of Piacenza.—He grants that, while exiled from his church, he may retain both vacant prebends and those about to become vacant. (18 December.) 488

CLXXVI.—To the nobleman Count Guido.—By apostolic authority he confirms the judgment rendered in the case between him and the elect and sisters of the monastery of Rosano. (20 December.) 489

CLXXVII.—To the bishop of Autun.—That clerics or laymen are not withdrawn from the bishop’s jurisdiction by letters of protection. (13 December.) 489

CLXXVIII.—To the bishop of Padua.—That he compel monks who have left to return to their cloisters. (23 December.) 490

CLXXIX.—To Odo, bishop of Paris.—From eleven prebends of the church of Champeaux he grants him authority to create twenty-two. (30 December.) 490

CLXXX.—To the prior and monks of Lenton.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (6 January.) 491

CLXXXI.—To the same.—On the same subject. (7 January.) 492

CLXXXII.—To the bishop of London.—He confirms the dignity of the Church of London. (13 December.) 492

CLXXXIII.—To the archpriest of Autun, the prior of Saint Symphorian in the diocese of Autun, and Master R. de Dencevoi, canon of Dijon in the diocese of Langres.—He commands them to ensure observance of the judgment rendered in the case between the abbot and monks of Clairvaux on one side, and the monks of Saint-Bénigne of Dijon on the other. 493

CLXXXIV.—To the abbot of the monastery of Saint Vincent of Le Mans.—He receives the monastery of Saint Vincent of Le Mans under the protection of Saint Peter, and the possessions belonging to that monastery are enumerated. (9 January.) 494

CLXXXV.—To Hugh of Saint Peter of Cluny.—He confirms the privileges which are enumerated, together with its appurtenances. (13 January.) 497

CLXXXVI.—To the king of France.—That he restrain the insolence of Jews dwelling in the kingdom and rise up against heretics. (16 January.) 501

CLXXXVII.—To the bishop and canons of Feltre.—He confirms the statute establishing ten canons in their church. (9 January.) 503

CLXXXVIII.—To the same.—He confirms their privileges. 504

CLXXXIX.—To the illustrious king of Armenia.—That he make satisfaction for the injuries he inflicted upon the brethren of the military order of the Temple. (18 January.) 504

CXC.—To Richard, abbot of Compiègne.—He grants the use of the mitre and ring. (18 January.) 504

CXCI.—To the prior of Camaldoli and Master Gualand, canon of Pisa.—Concerning the translation of the bishopric of Fiesole. (20 January.) 505

CXCII.—To the bishop of Olomouc.—He writes in favour of P., who had been promoted to the order of priesthood while omitting the rank of deacon. (21 January.) 505

CXCIII.—To the bishop of Chalon and the abbot of Cluny.—He commits to them the examination of the election of the abbot of Saint Martin of Troyes. (20 January.) 506

CXCIV.—To Master Peter, priest of Saint Columba.—That he not permit the serfs of his parish to live with Jews. (20 January.) 507

CXCV.—To the bishop of Chartres.—That, where the trustees of deceased persons fail to carry out their will, he himself carry it out. (24 January.) 507

CXCVI.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—He commits to him alone for judgment the case concerning the parish of Bujan. (26 January.) 508

CXCVII.—To the dean and chapter of Beauvais.—That, so long as their bishop is willing to obey the law, they do not cease divine offices against him. [Col. 1630] (23 January.) 508

CXCVIII.—To the bishop of Beauvais.—Commission for collecting tithes, including those of wool, lambs, produce, and hay. (24 January.) 509

CXCIX.—To the brethren of the hospital of Saint James of Colle Bertanni.—He receives them under protection, subject to an annual payment of one bezant. (27 January.) 509

CC.—To the bishop of Ferrara.—That he go to Venice and inquire concerning the consecration of the patriarch-elect of Grado. (28 January.) 509

CCI.—From Emperor Baldwin to the pope.—He requests confirmation of the agreements concluded between himself and the Venetians. 510

CCII.—From the doge of Venice to the pope.—He excuses himself concerning the destruction of Zadar and gives an account of the capture of Constantinople; thereafter he asks that the petitions which he makes through messengers be graciously heard. 511

CCIII.—To the bishops, abbots, and other clerics at Constantinople.—He rejoices at the return of the Church of Constantinople to obedience to the Apostolic See; declaring void the patriarchal election made by them, he himself elects the same man by apostolic authority. (21 January.) 512

CCIV.—To B., illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—Concerning confirmation of the patriarch of Constantinople. (21 January.) 517

CCV.—Instrument of agreement between the counts of Flanders, etc., the marquis of Montferrat, and the Venetians. (March.) 517

CCVI.—To the nobleman, the doge of Venice.—He answers his request that the agreements concluded between the Franks and Venetians be confirmed. (29 January.) 519

CCVII.—To the nobleman H., doge of Venice.—He confirms his absolution. (29 January.) 521

CCVIII.—To B., illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—He annuls the agreements concerning the division of ecclesiastical possessions. 521

CCIX.—To the chapter of Viviers.—Concerning the resignation made by their bishop and the holding of a new election. (20 January.) 523

CCX.—To Brother P. of Castronovo, legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the patient and vigorous exercise of his legation. (26 January.) 525

CCXI.—To the abbot of Cluny.—He grants him authority, in abbeys belonging to the monastery of Cluny, to correct what requires correction according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. (29 January.) 526

CCXII.—To the king of France.—Concerning the extirpation of heretics. (7 February.) 526

CCXIII.—To the bishop of Tournai.—He exhorts him and grants powers to restrain the offences of clerics. (7 February.) 528

CCXIV.—To the same.—Authority to perform dedications for churches, both on Sundays and on private days. (7 February.) 528

CCXV.—To N. …—He commits the case between the brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem and the abbess of Saint Mary of Angers concerning an alms-house. (8 February.) 528

CCXVI.—To the bishop of Avranches and the abbots of Montmorel and La Lucerne.—He commits to them the examination of the case between the prior and canons of Saint Barbara on one side, and W., chamberlain of Tancarville in the diocese of Rouen, on the other, concerning Mainerius of Monville. (10 February.) 529

CCXVII.—To the abbot of Molesme.—Concerning letters of confirmation. (9 February.) 530

CCXVIII.—To the prior and brethren of Val-des-Choux.—He receives them under the protection of Saint Peter. (10 February.) 531

CCXIX.—To the bishop of Aquitani [reading uncertain].—He settles a dispute between R. de Georgio and R., a woman of Saint-Germain. (12 February.) 532

CCXX.—To the bishops of Ely, Norwich, and Saint Asaph.—That they settle the matrimonial case between the daughter of the prince of the Isles and the prince of North Wales. (17 February.) 534

CCXXI.—To the prior of the monastery of Blessed Mary of La Charité and his brethren.—Confirmation of privileges and enumeration of everything belonging to them. (16 February.) 537

CCXXII.—To the bishop of Vercelli.—He admonishes and requests concerning the patriarchate of Jerusalem. (17 February.) 540

CCXXIII.—To P., cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, legate of the Apostolic See.—He rebukes him because, together with the cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, he left the Holy Land and went to Constantinople. Nevertheless, he commands that, while in that city, he arrange everything there until the arrival of another legate, without meanwhile neglecting the care of affairs in Jerusalem. [Col. 1631] (17 February.) 541

CCXXIV.—To all Christ’s faithful established throughout Lombardy.—He declares that persons excommunicated by the Apostolic See must not be regarded as absolved if letters are directed to them by the pope with a form of greeting. (21 February.) 542

CCXXV.—To the bishops of Piacenza and Tortona.—Authority to absolve the people of Piacenza. (21 February.) 542

CCXXVI.—Letter of Andrew, governor of Hungary.—Concerning the translation of the archbishop of Kalocsa to the archbishopric of Esztergom. 543

CCXXVII.—To the abbots of La Cour-Dieu and La Charité, in the dioceses of Orléans and Chartres, and to the cantor of Orléans.—He commits to them the case between W., viscount of Benaix, and his wife Eustachia. (17 February.) 544

CCXXVIII.—To the podestà and people of Ancona.—That they resist the intruded archbishop of Mainz. 548

CCXXIX.—Order for the coronation of Peter, king of Aragon. (10 November.) 550

CCXXX.—Letter of Kaloyan, king of Bulgaria, to the pope.—He reports the arrival of the legate, from whom he subsequently received a crown, and sends him certain gifts. 551

CCXXXI.—Letter of Basil, primate of the Bulgarians, to the pope.—He reports that he was endowed with sacred anointing by the cardinal legate. 553

## BOOK EIGHTH

Eighth year of the pontificate; A.D. 1205.

I.—To the abbots of Lucedio and Mount Tabor, and to the noblemen Count Berthold and G. de Fornivall.—He commits to them for judgment the case between the king of Armenia and the count of Tripoli concerning the principality of Antioch. (5 March.) 555

II.—To L., illustrious king of the Armenians.—On the same subject as in the preceding letter. (5 March.) 557

III.—To the abbots of Hétouard and Heggen, and the provost of Gusmaria, in the dioceses of Paderborn and Mainz.—He commits to them for judgment the case concerning the election of the abbess of the church of Heris. (2 March.) 559

IV.—To the prior and monks of the monastery of Winchester, present and future, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (3 March.) 561

V.—To the archbishop of Canterbury and the bishops of Ely and London.—That the king of England permit the monks of Winchester freely to proceed to the election of a bishop. (9 March.) 562

VI.—To the bishop of Ely, the abbot of Saint Edmund, and the dean of Chichester.—That they grant the archbishop of York absolution from the sentence of excommunication pronounced against him for violent laying of hands upon clerics. (26 February.) 563

VII.—To the archbishop of Rouen and the bishops of Avranches, Lisieux, Coutances, and Séez.—They are instructed that, concerning the rendering of fealty by them to the king of France, they are to do what is customary by law and usage. (7 March.) 564

VIII.—To the abbot of Bongar, the provost of Saint Arbogast in the diocese of Strasbourg, and the custos of Saint Thomas of Strasbourg.—He adjudicates the case concerning the church of Westhusen. (15 March.) 564

IX.—To the king of Aragon.—That he cease certain molestations of the Church of Elne. Many matters are added by which it is established that he is bound to preserve fidelity to the Roman Church. (12 March.) 568

X.—To G., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—He commands him at a provincial council to compel archdeacons and deans to receive sacred orders. (5 March.) 569

XI.—To the same.—That he not allow any regular abbot to stand surety. (7 March.) 570

XII.—To C., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—Authority to correct what requires correction in the monasteries of the province of Reims. (8 March.) 570

XIII.—To G., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—That he follow the statutes of the Lateran Council concerning vacant churches and prebends. (8 March.) 571

XIV.—To G., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—That he may revoke alienations unlawfully made there by his predecessors. (8 March.) 571

XV.—To G., archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—That he may revoke grants unlawfully made to his predecessors. (21 March.) 572

XVI.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—Concerning a certain oath not to reclaim usury. (15 March.) 572

[Col. 1632]

XVII.—To the bishop and the beloved sons, the cantor and archdeacon of Dol.—That they grant W., a priest whose genitals had been amputated in addition to wounds inflicted upon him, permission to perform the priestly office; and that they pronounce a sentence of excommunication against those who perpetrate such a crime. (28 March.) 573

XVIII.—To the bishop of Orvieto.—That in the matrimonial case between James, knight of Città della Pieve, and M., a woman, he may proceed notwithstanding a certain decretal of Pope Alexander, whose meaning is here explained. (21 March.) 573

XIX.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—He deals with the consecration of the patriarch of Constantinople. (30 March.) 574

XX.—To the same Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—He grants authority to absolve from censures incurred for striking a cleric, and commands him to anoint the emperor of Constantinople. (30 March.) 576

XXI.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—He grants authority to promote persons to orders and to appoint suitable men to ministries. (30 March.) 577

XXII.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—That, by the counsel of prudent men, he may decide concerning the goods of his church as he sees expedient, without having to refer these matters to the Apostolic See. (30 March.) 577

XXIII.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—He determines what is to be done in the election of patriarchs of the Church of Constantinople. (30 March.) 577

XXIV.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—He permits the retention of benefices and permits him to use the services of clerics who had accompanied him to those regions. (30 March.) 578

XXV.—To Thomas, patriarch of Constantinople.—That the rights of the Church of Constantinople are not derogated from because the pope himself elected the patriarch. (30 March.) 578

XXVI.—To the patriarch of Grado and his suffragans.—He informs him that he has decreed that clerics who are with the patriarch of Constantinople are not to lose their benefices. (30 March.) 579

XXVII.—To the prior and chapter of Saint Sylvanus of Leproso.—He receives them under the protection of Saint Peter, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (23 February.) 580

XXVIII.—To the abbots of Saint Julian and Turpiniac, and Master Bald…, canon of Saint Martin of Tours.—He commits to them for decision the case of Master Peter of Vico concerning a prebend granted to him in the church of Bourges. (25 March.) 580

XXIX.—To the nobleman Matthew of Argent.—He confirms the judgment rendered by G., cardinal-deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico, in the case between him and John of Zita concerning certain land and a mill. (26 March.) 582

XXX.—To the bishop of Spoleto.—He annuls the judgment rendered against him in the case between him and the syndic of the Lateran Church concerning episcopal right in the church of Sciliana. (28 March.) 585

XXXI.—To the abbot of Saint Geneviève and the dean and chancellor of Paris.—He commits to them the case between the countess of Blois and the chapter of the Church of Chartres concerning the capture of a thief. (1 April.) 586

XXXII.—To the abbot of the monastery of Saint Peter of Chalon and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under protection, and the possessions belonging to them are enumerated. (27 March.) 590

XXXIII.—To the bishop of Worcester, the abbot of Chichester, and the dean of York.—Concerning the church of Wdehord, not to be assigned to the nephew of the bishop of St Albans. (24 March.) 591

XXXIV.—To the bishop of Ely, the archdeacon of Cambridge, and the prior of Barnoeta in the diocese of Ely.—He commits a matrimonial case to them. (9 April.) 593

XXXV.—To the bishop of Dol and the abbots of Savigny and Ardenne.—He commits to them the case of the election of the bishop of Bayeux. (22 April.) 594

XXXVI.—To Duke Andrew, governor of the kingdom of Hungary.—He replies to his letter and commends to him Ladislaus, the boy king, his ward and nephew. (25 April.) 595

XXXVII.—To the same.—That he ensure the distribution of the money which the deceased king had left to certain persons. (25 April.) 596

XXXVIII.—To the same.—That he pay the revenues which he had promised to the king and to the king’s mother, the queen. (25 April.) 596

XXXIX.—To the same and to all princes established in the same kingdom.—He admonishes them to care for the boy king in such a way that they dare under no circumstances alienate royal possessions. [Col. 1633] (25 April.) 597

XL.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, provosts, other prelates and princes, the clergy, and all the people of the kingdom of Hungary.—He commands them altogether to keep faith with the king. (25 April.) 597

XLI.—To the archbishop of Kalocsa and the bishop of Várad.—He enjoins upon them the task of restraining those who harass King Ladislaus and the household of his queen. (27 April.) 597

XLII.—To the suffragans of the Church of Kalocsa.—He commands them to remain faithful to the boy king. (25 April.) 598

XLIII.—To Abbess M. and the sisters of Gandersheim.—He renews and confirms the privileges granted to them by Pope Agapetus II and Pope John XIII. (The papal diplomas are inserted.) (2 May.) 598

XLIV.—To the abbots of Pöhlde, Corvey, and Saint Michael’s Stone, in the dioceses of Merseburg, Paderborn, and Halberstadt.—He gives them the task of investigating the subjection of the monastery of Gandersheim to the Church of Hildesheim. (3 May.) 603

XLV.—To the bishop of Arras, the abbot of Saint Bertin in the diocese of Thérouanne, and S. of Vallibus, canon of Laon.—He commits to them examination of the election of the bishop of Amiens. (2 May.) 605

XLVI.—To the archbishop of Kalocsa.—Concerning the restoration to devotion toward the Apostolic See of a certain bishopric, said here to be in the land of the sons of Beoknese. (3 May.) 610

XLVII.—To the prior and canons of Saint Peter of Turgarcan.—He adjudicates to them the churches of Ttihebi and Wetorp [otherwise, Duthorpe]. (30 April.) 611

XLVIII.—To W., lord of Guirchia.—He receives him under the protection of Saint Peter, subject to an annual payment of one bezant. (1 May.) 616

XLIX.—To the woman Alferada.—He receives under protection the church founded by her. (11 May.) 616

L.—To the king of Castile.—He rebukes him because Jews and Saracens are held in honour by him. (5 May.) 616

LI.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—In reply to his question whether he could dispense concerning a marriage, ignorantly contracted in the sixth degree of consanguinity, he answers that it may be overlooked. (10 May.) 618

LII.—To the archbishop of Sens.—Permission is granted for him to visit the province of Sens and correct what requires correction. (12 May.) 618

LIII.—To the bishop of Tortona and Bono John, our subdeacon and canon of Vercelli.—He gives them the task of investigating the bishopric of Alessandria. (12 March.) 619

LIV.—To all abbots, priors, and others subject by diocesan law to the Church of Bourges.—That they not refuse to attend the synod once a year. (5 May.) 622

LV.—To the emperor of Constantinople.—He sends to the Greeks B., cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, legate *a latere* of the Apostolic See, and commends him to the emperor. (15 May.) 622

LVI.—To the archbishops, bishops, and all prelates established in the empire of Constantinople.—He commands that they receive the legate of the Apostolic See kindly and treat him honourably, and observe his ordinances. 624

LVII.—To the marquis of Montferrat.—That he love and honour the Roman Church. 624

LVIII.—Letter of the marquis of Montferrat.—In testimony of his love and obedience toward the Roman Church, he sends an envoy to the pope and informs him of events at Constantinople. 624

LIX.—To the abbot and convent of Casa Dei.—Concerning establishment of a bishopric in the city of Montispilosi. (18 May.) 624

LX.—To the bishop of Worcester, the abbot of Chichester, and the dean of York.—On the same subject as letter 33 of this eighth book. (16 May.) 625

LXI.—To the bishop, dean, and Master H., canon of Hildesheim.—Concerning the assignment to the cleric Daniel of a prebend in the church of Saint Willehad of Bremen. (19 May.) 626

LXII.—To B., cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Susanna, legate of the Apostolic See.—Permission is granted that, unless the patriarch of Constantinople appoint suitable men in the Church of Constantinople, he himself may appoint learned and honourable men in that church, as he considers expedient. (20 May.) 628

LXIII.—To all the clergy and people in the Christian army stationed at Constantinople.—He commands that they give the emperor of Constantinople aid and counsel concerning the recovery of the Holy Land. 629

LXIV.—To the patriarch and all the clergy of Constantinople.—He establishes that, whenever the Church of Constantinople becomes vacant, all prelates of the conventual churches situated at Constantinople are to assemble in the church of Saint Sophia to deliberate concerning the election. [Col. 1634] 629

LXV.—To the master and brethren of the house of the hospital of Saint Rainerius.—He receives their hospital into the right and ownership of Saint Peter. (25 May.) 629

LXVI.—To Savaric, bishop of Bath and Glastonbury.—He confirms the settlement of the Church of Glastonbury made by delegated judges. (The settlement is inserted.) (17 May.) 630

LXVII.—To the bishop of Mâcon and the abbot of Baume in the diocese of Besançon.—That they not permit P., a monk and administrator of Saint-Bénigne of Dijon, to be raised to a prelacy, since under his administration that church had been despoiled. (23 May.) 632

LXVIII.—To the archdeacon and abbot of Saint Faustino Maggiore of Brescia.—He writes in favour of the nuns of Saint Peter of the Bank at Brescia, so that Vitalis Humazolus may not harass them concerning usury. (28 May.) 633

LXIX.—To the archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans.—That he induce both clerics and laymen to go to the emperor of Constantinople, for the aid of the Holy Land and to fight the barbarians. 634

LXX.—To all archbishops and others in France.—He commands that from every order they send men commended for morals and learning to the regions of Greece, in order to establish the Christian faith there. (26 May.) 636

LXXI.—To the masters and scholars of Paris.—That they go to Greece in order to reform the study from which it had its beginning. 637

LXXII.—To the chapter of Soissons.—It is written that, since the presence of the bishop of Soissons in Greece is necessary for the recovery of the Holy Land, they should bear his absence humbly and devoutly. 638

LXXIII.—To all abbots, priors, and other religious persons to whom these letters shall come.—That they provide P., a monk sent by the emperor of Constantinople to the Apostolic See, with provisions. 639

LXXIV.—To the archbishop of Tuam, the bishop of Meath, and the abbot of Rahan.—That, in the dispute between the canons of Saint Mary of Luivid and H. de Say, knight, they determine what shall be just. (27 May.) 659

LXXV.—To Guy, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—Confirmation of his privileges, among which the chief is reckoned that he alone may anoint and crown the kings of France. (15 May.) 640

LXXVI.—To the archbishop of Arles and the abbots of Valmagne and Saint-Guilhem, in the dioceses of Agde and Lodève.—That they remove the bishop of Agde from his church and elect another. (25 May.) 642

LXXVII.—To the bishops of Minden and Verden, and the abbot of Verden.—That they grant the archbishop of Magdeburg the benefit of absolution, report on certain other matters, and write back. (25 May.) 644

LXXVIII.—To the abbots of Pöhlde and Saint Giles of Brunswick, in the dioceses of Halberstadt and Merseburg, and the dean of Merseburg.—He commits to them the case of the cleric A. concerning a prebend in the Church of Merseburg, formerly granted to him by the archbishop of Reims, then legate of the Apostolic See. (27 May.) 645

LXXIX.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—That he absolve the Carolitan judge from the oath made to him, enjoining him not to delay in swearing to the Roman Church. 647

LXXX.—To J., archpriest of Perugia.—He determines that he is not bound by anything decreed by a legate of the Apostolic See in the Church of Perugia contrary to privileges granted by the Apostolic See. (3 June.) 647

LXXXI.—To the patriarch of Aquileia.—He commands that he have the bishop of Padua investigate the parish priest of Gonew, accused of the crime of apostasy. (4 June.) 648

LXXXII.—To the abbots of Heisterbach and Rumersdorf and the dean of Bonn, in the diocese of Cologne.—He commands them to investigate whether peace can be restored between two counts through a marriage between the parties, although they are related within a certain degree of affinity. (4 June.) 649

LXXXIII.—To the patriarch of Aquileia and the abbot of Neuburg.—He commands them to admonish the duke of Swabia not to give any aid to the excommunicated bishop of Worms. (4 June.) 650

LXXXIV.—To the same.—That they place the duke of Swabia under interdict from sacred rites unless he repent within the prescribed time. (4 June.) 653

LXXXV.—To all the people of Viterbo: a spirit of sounder counsel.—That they rise against certain Patarenes and provide them neither aid, counsel, nor favour. [Col. 1635]

LXXXVI.—To the clerics of Saint Agatha.—They are restored to receipt of a certain annual pension in the church of Saint Saviour, and the priest is condemned to payment of that pension. (4 June.) 657

LXXXVII.—To G., senior archdeacon, Master R., penitentiary of Saint Victor of Paris, and Master R. de Corzon, canon of Noyon residing at Paris.—He commands them to absolve the bishop of Toul from the bond of excommunication and to determine the case between that bishop and the archdeacon of Toul. (7 June.) 659

LXXXVIII.—To Andrew, lord of Hungary.—He gives the reason why he does not comply with Andrew’s request that the archbishop of Kalocsa be made archbishop of Esztergom, and commands another to be elected. (25 May.) 661

LXXXIX.—To the prior and brethren of the hospital of the Holy Trinity of Vernolio.—He receives them under protection, subject to an annual payment of one gold obol. (11 June.) 662

XC.—To S., archbishop of Mainz.—Concerning the consecration of the bishop of Strasbourg. (6 June.) 662

XCI.—To the consuls and people of Montpellier.—That they not impede the construction of the oratory of the Holy Spirit; a threatening letter. (3 June.) 664

XCII.—To P., king of Aragon.—He grants to him and his successors that they be crowned at Saragossa by the archbishop of Tarragona. (16 June.) 665

XCIII.—To the same.—He promises that, if he obtains the island of Majorca, an episcopal see shall be established there. 666

XCIV.—To the same.—He grants him authority lawfully to possess whatever he can acquire from the land of heretics. 666

XCV.—To the archbishops, bishops, and prelates established throughout the land of Aragon.—He commands them to stand ready with aid and counsel for the king in expelling the ungodly. 666

XCVI.—To the brethren of Calatrava and Vélez.—He commands them to assist the king of Aragon against the Saracens. (5 July.) 666

XCVII.—To the abbot of Cîteaux, P. of Castronovo, and Master R., legates of the Apostolic See.—That they grant in fief to the king of Aragon the Castle of Scura, which is the property of Saint Peter, recovered from heretics by that king, at an annual payment to be set at their discretion. (16 June.) 667

XCVIII.—To the bishop of Cenad and the abbot of Stekedor of the Cistercian Order.—That they receive the purgation of the bishop of Pécs concerning the accusation of incest. (20 May.) 667

XCIX.—To S., bishop of Bath and Glastonbury.—A delay is granted for crossing the sea. (21 June.) 668

C.—To B., master, and the brethren of Saint Julian of Perario, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—He receives them under the protection of Saint Peter, subject to an annual payment of one maravedí. (16 June.) 668

CI.—To all archbishops and prelates established in the province of Jerusalem.—That they receive humbly and devoutly the legate of the Apostolic See sent to the kingdom of Jerusalem. 669

CII.—To the patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See.—Authority to grant the benefit of absolution to all who cross the sea, however and by whomever they have been excommunicated. (29 December.) 670

CIII.—To the same.—That clerics crossing the sea with him may receive the fruits of their prebends for three years. (29 December.) 670

CIV.—To the convent of Winchester and the abbots, priors, and all the clergy of the diocese of Winchester.—He confirms the election of the precentor of Lincoln as bishop of Winchester. (21 June.) 671

CV.—To the bishops of Viterbo and Orvieto.—That they exercise the authority granted them against the Patarenes; they are to go to Viterbo and remove the elected consuls from office. (16 June.) 673

CVI.—To the archbishop of Narbonne.—He commands him to present himself before the apostolic presence and clear himself of the charges brought against him. (26 June.) 674

CVII.—To Duke Andrew, governor of the kingdom of Hungary.—He gives the reason why he does not assent to Andrew’s requests concerning the bishopric of Bamberg. 675

CVIII.—To the provost, dean, and chapter of the Church of Halberstadt; to the prelates and all clergy established in the diocese of Halberstadt; and to all faithful of the Church of Halberstadt.—He informs them that the bishop of Halberstadt has been absolved from the bond of excommunication and commands them to render him due reverence and honour. (26 June.) 676

CIX.—To the provost of Würzburg, the provost of Husdorp, and the dean of Saint Mary at Herford in the diocese of Mainz.—That they ensure that Master Martin enjoys peaceful possession of the prebend conferred upon him by the Apostolic See in the Church of Minden. [Col. 1636] (13 June.) 676

CX.—To the archbishop and the abbots of Saint Remigius and Saint John of Sens.—That they receive from H., deacon of Sens, the resignation of a certain benefice, notwithstanding that the diocesan bishop had promised that benefice after the death of the said deacon. (9 June.) 678

CXI.—To the provost, dean, and scholastic of Bourges in the diocese of Cologne.—That they admonish and induce E. de Hard., and also compel him by ecclesiastical censure, to receive G., his wife, notwithstanding the unlawful oath made by the spouses,
that henceforth neither party shall make a claim against the other. (2 July.) 678

CXII.—To the Archbishop of Sens, the Abbot of Saint Marianus, and Master R. de Corzon.—That they inquire into the accusation which O., Duke of Burgundy, was bringing concerning the marriage of one of his kinswomen to the Count of Nevers, on the ground that they were related to one another in the fourth degree of consanguinity, and report to the Apostolic See. (5 July.) 679

CXIII.—To the Queen of the Franks.—He consoles her in her grief by letter and embassy. (5 July.) 680

CXIV.—To the Archbishop of Armagh, the Bishop of Down, and the Abbot of Inis in the diocese of Down.—That, if H. de Lacy has unjustly made war against John de Courcy, they are to make him restore what he has occupied. (1 July.) 681

CXV.—To R., former Bishop of Toulouse.—He grants that, although he has resigned the administration of the Church of Toulouse, he may exercise episcopal office, without prejudice to another. (5 July.) 682

CXVI.—To the Abbot of Cîteaux, R., and P., monks of Fontfroide, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they remove Mascaron from the provostship of Toulouse. (6 July.) 683

CXVII.—To Bertrand, Bishop of Agen, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—He receives him under the protection of blessed Peter and confirms the privileges granted him by the King of England. (2 July.) 684

CXVIII.—To B., Archbishop of Trani, legate of the Apostolic See.—He confirms a dispensation concerning Bartholomew, a deacon, who did not know whether he had received the lower orders, and orders that the minor orders be conferred upon him as a precaution. (7 July.) 686

CXIX.—Letter of Leo, King of the Armenians, to the Pope.—He informs the Pope that peace has been restored between himself and the Templars, and concerning certain other matters. 687

CXX.—A letter sent through the Catholicos of the Armenians to Pope Innocent III.—On the same subject and on certain other matters. 692

CXXI.—To the Archbishop of Sens and the Bishop of Paris.—That they restrain the insolence of the Jews. (15 July.) 694

CXXII.—Instrument.—By which William, marquis, son of Marquis Pelavicini, promises to obey the commands of the Pope. (31 March.) 695

CXXIII.—Instrument.—By which the same marquis, to obtain absolution, delivers the castle of Landasia to the Bishop of Modena in full ownership, and receives investiture of it from him. (22 March.) 696

CXXIV.—To the Bishops of Modena and Reggio.—He orders that what they had done in absolving William Pelavicini shall stand ratified. (20 July.) 696

CXXV.—To N. … (The address is missing.)—That they induce King Philip of France to assist the Holy Land. 698

CXXVI.—To Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, legate of the Apostolic See.—He rebukes the legate for having deserted the Holy Land, etc. (10 July.) 699

CXXVII.—To A., illustrious King of Hungary.—That he cause to be restored to G., clerk of the Bishop of Porto, the things which had been taken from him. (27 July.) 702

CXXVIII.—To the Abbot and convent of Albarens.—He orders them to confirm the election of Andrew, provost of Saint Nicholas of Corneto, as abbot of Saint Augustine of Monte-Albo. 703

CXXIX.—To Kalojan, King of the Bulgarians and Vlachs.—That he make peace with the Latins and free the Emperor of Constantinople, whom he holds captive. 705

CXXX.—To all Christ’s faithful wishing to proceed to Constantinople in aid of the Holy Land.—That they make the Pope aware of their purpose. (16 August.) 706

CXXXI.—Letter of Henry, brother of the Emperor.—He informs him that Emperor Baldwin has been captured by the Bulgarians, and sends envoys. (5 June.) 706

CXXXII.—To Henry, brother of the Emperor of Constantinople.—That he establish and confirm peace with the King of Bulgaria. 710

[Col. 1637]

CXXXIII.—To the Marquis of Montferrat.—That he defend and protect the subjugated Empire of Constantinople until the Pope is better informed whether this was done unjustly. 710

CXXXIV.—To M. …, wife of the nobleman B., Marquis of Montferrat, formerly Empress of Constantinople.—He congratulates her that, having cast aside Greek rites, she had embraced the Latins. 714

CXXXV.—To B., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he confirm certain ordinances in the Church of Constantinople, in accordance with the agreements made. 715

CXXXVI.—To the Patriarch of Constantinople.—That he not delay to have Henry, a clerk, received as a canon of the Church of Saint Sophia. (7 September.) 715

CXXXVII.—To Frederick, provost of Clarholz.—A dispensation for defect of birth, enabling him to receive dignities. 715

CXXXVIII.—To the Archbishop of Mainz.—That he confer consecration upon the Bishop-elect of Strasbourg; if he delays in doing so, the matter is committed to the Archbishop of Sens. (8 October.) 716

CXXXIX.—To the Provost and chapter of Strigonia.—He appoints the Archbishop of Kalocsa as their archbishop. (6 October.) 717

CXL.—To the Chapter of Kalocsa.—He declares that no harm shall be done to any of their rights by the translation of the archbishop. (14 October.) 720

CXLI.—To Henry and Vitalis of Collisvacone, canons of Benevento.—That they too regard as legitimate a certain person whom the Apostolic See has declared legitimate, and in the case concerning his inheritance proceed according to the tenor of apostolic letters. (15 October.) 721

CXLII.—To P., Bishop of Winchester.—That in monasteries and churches subject to him by diocesan law he correct what needs correction. (27 October.) 722

CXLIII.—To the same.—That he may revoke things unlawfully alienated. (27 October.) 722

CXLIV.—To the same.—That he may compel archdeacons and deans, etc., to receive orders. (27 October.) 722

CXLV.—To the same.—That he compel those who obtain ecclesiastical personages (personatus) to appoint vicars willing and able to perform personal service. (27 October.) 722

CXLVI.—To the same.—That he correct clerical offences. (27 October.) 723

CXLVII.—To the same.—That he remove sons of priests. (27 October.) 723

CXLVIII.—To the same.—That he prevent the alternation of benefices. (27 October.) 724

CXLIX.—To the same; to the Bishops of London and Worcester, and the Dean of Chichester.—That they restore innovations in the Church of Winchester to their proper state. (27 October.) 724

CL.—To the Archbishop, the Dean, and the Archdeacon of Bourges.—That, if the Archbishop of Bordeaux refuses to resign pastoral government, they remove him and enjoin the chapter to elect another suitable person as pastor. (31 October.) 724

CLI.—To the same.—He grants him authority to absolve his servants and clerics of his church from violent assault. (12 November.) 725

CLII.—To B., Archdeacon of Vienne, our subdeacon.—He grants him, elected Bishop of Viviers, authority to retain other ecclesiastical benefices besides the archdeaconry of Vienne. (5 November.) 726

CLIII.—To T., Patriarch of Constantinople.—He orders him not to delay consecrating the Bishop-elect of Patras and investing him with the honour of the pallium. (19 November.) 727
