CLIV.—To the Bishops of Rochester and London, and the Prior of Saint Alban’s in the diocese of London.—He commits to them the case concerning the church of Faversham between the Abbot of Saint Augustine’s and the Archdeacon of Canterbury. (21 November.) 727

CLV.—To the Bishops of Rochester and London, and the Prior of Saint Alban’s in the diocese of London.—On the same matter; and that they compel the Archdeacon of Canterbury to restore a certain altar. (24 November.) 729

CLVI.—To the Bishop of Florence.—That he receive the canons as witnesses in the case between the Bishop and chapter of Volterra. (27 November.) 734

CLVII.—To the Bishop of Ferrara, the Abbot of Colomba, and the Archdeacon of Verona.—That they establish a definite rule for the monastery of Castanasio. (25 November.) 734

CLVIII.—To the Bishop of Basel and the Abbot of Salem.—That, on coming to the monastery of Reichenau, they procure the election of a suitable person as abbot. (5 December.) 735

CLIX.—To C., priest-cardinal, and the clerics of Saint Lawrence in Lucina.—A certain agreement between them is confirmed. (7 December.) 738

CLX.—To the Abbot and convent of Saint Peter of Culture, in the diocese of Le Mans.—All pensions made or promised by R., former abbot, are annulled. (30 November.) 739

CLXI.—To the Abbots of Saint Alban’s in the diocese of Lincoln and of Radinges in the diocese of Salisbury, and the Dean of Saint Paul’s, London.—That they hear witnesses in the case of the Archbishop-elect of Canterbury. (11 December.) 740

CLXII.—To the Bishop of Florence.—That he restore a fief to certain nobles who stood for the Church during the time of schism. (12 December.) 740

CLXIII.—To the Bishops of London and Ely, and the Abbot of Saint Edmund’s in the diocese of Norwich.—That, in the case between the Archdeacon of Canterbury on one side and the abbot and monks of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury, on the other, concerning possession of the guardianship of the church of Middleton, they hear witnesses. (12 December.) 742

CLXIV.—To the Bishop and Dean of Lincoln.—That they may dispense G., son of Peter, Justiciar of England, from a pilgrimage vow for three years. (16 December.) 743

CLXV.—To the Abbot of Vallombrosa and Master Gualando, our subdeacon and canon of Pisa.—Concerning the transfer of the see of Fiesole to a suitable place. (16 December.) 745

CLXVI.—To the illustrious King of England.—That he not allow the nuns of the Holy Trinity at Caen to be summoned before lay judges. (23 December.) 747

CLXVII.—To Hamelin, Abbot of the monastery of Vendôme, and his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.—He receives it under the protection of blessed Peter, subject to an annual payment of twelve solidi, and enumerates the possessions belonging to it. (23 December.) 747

CLXVIII.—To the Bishop of Vercelli.—That he dissolve the marriage between Opizo Lancavecla and Rufuna, because the said O. was insane. (28 December.) 747

CLXIX.—To the Patriarch of Jerusalem.—A dispensation to visit the thresholds of the holy Apostles even through envoys. (29 December.) 751

CLXX.—To the same.—That the four-year term of his legation be reckoned from the day on which the church entrusted to him received him. (29 December.) 751

CLXXI.—To the same.—That he may use the pallium in any province. (29 December.) 752

CLXXII.—To the same.—That he may absolve from the bond of excommunication those wishing to cross overseas with him. (30 December.) 752

CLXXIII.—To the same.—He sends him money. (29 December.) 752

CLXXIV.—To the Archbishop-elect of Cologne.—That he may retain for two years the benefices which he had previously held. (29 December.) 753

CLXXV.—To the same.—That, if his suffragans neglect to initiate him in the sacred episcopal rites, he may summon other bishops for that purpose. (23 December.) 753

CLXXVI.—To the aldermen and all the people of Cologne.—Their ancient liberties are confirmed. (23 December.) 753

CLXXVII.—To the Chapter and clergy of Cologne.—Confirmation of the Archbishop-elect of Cologne. 754

CLXXVIII.—To all prelates throughout England.—That they ensure that Peter’s Pence, collected faithfully in England but not reaching the Roman pontiff intact through the deceit of officials, be levied every year and conveyed to him without any fraud. 754

CLXXIX.—To Peter, Bishop of Winchester.—That he may not be excommunicated without consultation with the Roman pontiff. (29 December.) 754

CLXXX.—To the Archbishop and B., cellarer of Tours.—He commits to them the case between J. … de Meduan and E. …, a noblewoman. (30 December.) 754

CLXXXI.—To Rainerius, treasurer of Nîmes.—He confirms to him the treasury of the Church of Nîmes. (13 December.) 755

CLXXXII.—To the cantor …, Sigibert, and M. de Saint-Quentin, canons of Noyon.—He commits to them the case between A., clerk of Noyon, and A. de Maisnil, knight. (30 December.) 756

CLXXXIII.—To the Patriarch of Aquileia.—That, during the absence of its pastor, he protect and defend the Church of Trent against the Count of Tyrol. (11 January.) 758

CLXXXIV.—To the same.—Authority to unite the bishoprics of Aemona and Justinopolis. (11 January.) 759

[Col. 1639]

CLXXXV.—To Ric., Dean of Salisbury.—A dispensation for defect of birth, enabling him to obtain benefices. (14 January.) 759

CLXXXVI.—To the Archpriest and canons of Saint Peter’s.—He urges observance of the statutes concerning the canons of Saint Peter’s. (11 January.) 760

CLXXXVII.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches to whom these letters shall come.—That the election of the Dean of Salisbury is annulled because of a defect in the election, not because of a defect in the person. (31 December.) 761

CLXXXVIII.—To G., Dean of Soissons, the cantor of Reims, and the subchanter of Senlis.—He commits to them the case concerning obedience between the Bishop of Meaux and the monastery of Rebais. (13 January.) 762

CLXXXIX.—To the Bishop of Brescia.—He answers his various inquiries. 765

CXC.—To the clergy and people throughout the diocese of Fermo.—That they render obedience to their bishop-elect. 767

CXCI.—To the Bishop-elect of Fermo and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—He grants immunities and privileges to him and his successors. 767

CXCII.—From the King of the Danes to the Pope.—He brings various complaints against Waldemar, Bishop of Schleswig, and asks that provision be made lest Denmark be disturbed by Waldemar. 768

CXCIII.—To the illustrious King of Denmark.—He urges him to clemency toward Waldemar and asks that he may be conducted under safe-conduct to the King of Hungary; he then promises to provide for the tranquillity of that kingdom. (20 January.) 771

CXCIV.—To the Archbishop of Lund.—That he visit the province of Lund and correct what needs correction. (18 January.) 773

CXCV.—To the same.—He answers his inquiry concerning a certain matrimonial case. (12 January.) 773

CXCVI.—To the same.—He confirms certain institutions made by him. (19 January.) 774

CXCVII.—To the same.—That in a city which he has brought back to the worship of the faith he may ordain a bishop. (13 January.) 775

CXCVIII.—To the same.—That an ordinance made by him concerning the condition of monks of the black order be observed. (18 January.) 775

CXCIX.—To the Abbot of Bardeslera, the Prior of the Holy Sepulchre, and the Dean of the diocese of Worcester.—That proceedings be conducted in the case between R., rector of the church of Saint Saldatus, on one side, and Thomas, rector of the chapel of Saint John of Glovernia, on the other, unless the plaintiff has become a member of the judge’s household. (27 January.) 775

CC.—To the Bishop of Vercelli, the Abbot of Tileto, etc., and Albert, priest of Mantua.—How and in what manner they ought to proceed against the Bishops of Novara and Ivrea. The resignations of the Bishops of Asti and Verona are also treated. (29 January.) 776

CCI.—To the Bishop of Worcester.—That, except on the day of the Lord’s Nativity, it is sufficient for a priest to celebrate one Mass. (26 January.) 777

CCII.—To the Dean of Saint Thomas of Crépy, in the diocese of Senlis, and Gerindus de Crech of Soissons and M. Gir. de Saint-Denis of Noyon, canons.—He commits to them the case between the Bishop of Meaux and the Abbess of Jouarre. (28 January.) 781

CCIII.—To the Archbishop of Toledo and the Bishop of Zamora.—That they compel the Kings of Castile and León to restore certain towns and possessions to the brothers of the Hospital of Jerusalem. (28 January.) 781

CCIV.—To the Abbot and brothers of Evesham Abbey.—He decides the case between it and the Bishop of Worcester concerning jurisdiction. (18 January.) 782

CCV.—To the Bishops of Ely and Rochester and Master B. of London.—On the same subject. (3 February.) 784

CCVI.—To the same.—On the same subject. (7 February.) 788

CCVII.—To the Bishop of Rochester.—That he persevere in government and not seek resignation. (1 February.) 789

CCVIII.—To the Prior of Saint Victor’s, Paris, Simon, subchanter of Senlis, and Master S. de Languet, theologian residing at Paris.—He commits to them the case between the Abbess of Foote[l] and the Abbot of Saint-Denis in France. (2 February.) 790

CCIX.—To J., cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.—He orders him to restrain the King of England from inflicting injuries upon the Dean of Salisbury and others. (1 February.) 791

CCX.—To the Prior of Saint Victor’s, Paris, Simon, subchanter of Senlis, and Master S. de Languet, theologian residing at Paris.—On the same subject as in Letter 45 of Book V. (1 February.) 792

CCXI.—To our faithful people and the people of Radicofani.—Authority to elect consuls. 793

CCXII.—To N., Dean, and the chapter of Le Mans.—He decides the case between them and the chapter of Saint Peter of Curia concerning the observance of an interdict imposed by the Bishop or chapter of Le Mans. (2 February.) 795

CCXIII.—To the canons of Saint Peter of Curia at Le Mans.—On the same subject. (1 February.) 796

CCXIV.—To the Archbishop of Nidaros and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.—He confirms his ancient privileges and grants. (13 February.) 797

CCXV.—To the same.—Authority to absolve persons excommunicated for violent assault upon clerics. (18 February.) 798

CCXVI.—To the same.—That no one may consecrate bishops in his metropolitan see unless authority has been granted by him. (11 February.) 800

## Book Nine

In the ninth year of the pontificate, A.D. 1265.

I.—To the Bishop of Cagliari.—That he not seek resignation; and the grounds on which a bishop is compelled to renounce and resign a bishopric are set forth. (1 March.) 801

II.—To the Archbishops of Toledo and Compostela.—He orders them to endeavour to settle the disputes which the Kings of Castile and León were pursuing concerning certain towns. 810

III.—To the Archbishop of Braga.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that the vigils of the Apostles are fast days, and other doubts are resolved. (21 February.) 810

IV.—To the Archbishop of Braga.—That the beating of clerics, in satisfaction for injury inflicted upon others, according to the custom of the country, is forbidden. (23 February.) 812

V.—To the Archbishop of Nidaros.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that baptism is not true unless performed with water and by a priest. (1 March.) 812

VI.—To the Archbishop of Nidaros.—That he forbid his priests to bear arms and go about in lay dress. (1 March.) 812

VI.—To the Podestà and council of Florence.—That they avoid heretics and persevere in the faith. (5 March.) 813

VIII.—To the consuls and people of Prato.—He commends them for having expelled heretics from their territory. (4 March.) 813

IX.—To the Dean of Etton and the Prior of Aqua Bella in the diocese of Maurienne.—That they proceed in the case of Maurienne. (3 March.) 815

X.—To the Bishop of Maurienne.—That he may retain a certain pledge. (1 March.) 815

XI.—To the Archbishop of Lund.—That he send for absolution to the Servant of the servants [of God] serfs who lay hands on clerics, unless they have done so in order to withdraw themselves from the service of their lords. (13 January.) 815

XII.—To the Archbishop of Tours.—That he give ecclesiastical burial to the body of a young woman who threw herself from a bridge, not voluntarily but by accident, while fleeing to escape the hands of those pursuing her for a dishonourable end. (4 March.) 816

XIII.—To the Archbishop and O., Archdeacon, of Genoa.—That a dowry be assigned to the husband, to whom the dowry may be entrusted, since his wife’s body has been entrusted to him. (8 March.) 816

XIV.—To the Bishop of Bamberg.—A time-limit is granted for coming to receive absolution. 817

XV.—Instrument by which Echembert, Bishop of Bamberg, attests by a written bond that he will observe the fidelity and obedience promised to the Lord Pope. 818

XVI.—To the Archbishop of Tours, and the master and brothers of the Hospital of the Holy Spirit in Saxony.—A holding at Fonte Moron is annexed to their hospital. (8 March.) 818

XVII.—To the Abbot of Saint Columba of Sens.—He grants him authority to receive tithes from the produce of the land in his parishes. (10 March.) 818

XVIII.—To the Podestà and council of Faenza.—That they exclude the Poor Men of Lyons and the Paterines from their country and city. (10 March.) 819

XIX.—To the Abbots of Saint Proculus and Saint Stephen at Bologna.—That they restrain by ecclesiastical coercion the heretics called the Poor Men. (10 March.) 819

XX.—To the Bishop of Florence.—That he induce and compel the commune of Pisa not to occupy certain rights of the Marquis of Massa which are held from the Church. (14 March.) 820

[Col. 1641]

XXI.—To the Archbishop of Pisa.—On the same subject. 821

XXII.—To A., provost elected Archbishop of Magdeburg.—The election is confirmed and he is appointed pastor. (25 February.) 822

XXIII.—To the Abbot of Saint Victor’s, Paris, the Dean of Soissons, and Master R. de Corzon, canon of Noyon.—He commits to them the case concerning the election of the Bishop of Troyes. (19 March.) 822

XXIV.—To the Abbot and chapter of Châtillon.—In a necessary case it is lawful to swear even through religious persons. (21 March.) 823

XXV.—To the Prior and convent of Glastonbury.—That, if their church has not been properly provided for, they pursue their right at the Curia. (14 March.) 825

XXVI.—To J., cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he give the prior and convent of Glastonbury leave to elect an abbot. (25 March.) 827

XXVII.—To the Archbishop of Arles.—That he prescribe a suitable time-limit to offenders for pursuing appeals which they introduce solely to persist in their wrongdoing and evade ecclesiastical discipline. (18 March.) 828

XXVIII.—To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he confirm the agreement between the King of Cyprus and Count H., then lord of the kingdom of Jerusalem. (30 March.) 829

XXIX.—To the Bishop of Orléans.—That, after examining the truth, he allow R., a subdeacon, to exercise only clerical office, because, in repelling force by force, he had struck a layman. (24 March.) 829

XXX.—To the Archbishop of Compostela.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that the same rule applies to regular canons as to monks in matters of advocacies. (12 March.) 830

XXXI.—To the same.—A judgment given in the case between the Templars and the Church of Compostela is confirmed. (12 March.) 831

XXXII.—To the Bishops of Zamora and Salamanca.—That, in paying the vows owed to the Church of Compostela, the ancient measure be observed in a specified manner. (23 March.) 832

XXXIII.—To the Bishop of Ourense.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that the Lateran Council is to be observed concerning the last wills of canons; answers are also given to other doubts. (15 March.) 832

XXXIV.—To the Prior and convent of Canterbury.—That they come for examination to hear whether the provision made by their archbishop was bad, as they allege. (30 March.) 833

XXXV.—To the suffragans of the Church of Canterbury.—On the same subject. (30 March.) 834

XXXVI.—To the King of England.—On the same subject. (30 March.) 839

XXXVII.—To the Bishop of Rochester and the Abbot of Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury.—On the same subject. (30 March.) 839

XXXVIII.—To the scholasticus of Hildesheim and the custodian and scholasticus of Minden.—That they investigate, in a specified manner, the election of the abbess of Herford. (29 March.) 839

XXXIX.—To P., Bishop of Porto.—Authority to make a will. (4 April.) 840

XL.—To the Archdeacon, chancellor, and Dean of Saint Germanus of Auxerre, at Paris.—That they cause to be observed what had been judicially decided in the case between Walter de Picerel, acting for himself, and Hugh de Feverniac, prodean of Alveoli, concerning the church of Beavilla. (24 March.) 843

XLI.—To the Bishop of Vercelli, the Abbot of Tilieto, and Albert, priest of Mantua.—How and when a prelate ought to proceed in punishing the offences of his subjects. 844

XLII.—To the Bishop of Halberstadt.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that a monk who rang a bell which fell and killed a boy may be promoted in the monastery to higher orders. (5 April.) 848

XLIII.—To the Bishop of Florence.—That subdeacons of the Roman Church who have acquired a benefice on account of which they owe him obedience are not exempt from his obedience. (7 April.) 848

XLIV.—To the Abbot and convent of Pultariens.—Their ancient privilege is renewed. (8 April.) 849

XLV.—To the nobleman, the Marquis of Namur, and all Christ’s faithful wishing to proceed with him to Constantinople in aid of the Holy Land.—That they go to Constantinople. (10 April.) 850

[Col. 1642]

XLVI.—To the Bishops of Brixen, Freising, and Trieste.—That they hear the case between the Churches of Salzburg and Gurk, and induce the parties to concord. (11 April.) 854

XLVII.—To the Bishop of Tortosa.—That he restore the churches of Alchézar to the Bishop of Huesca. (13 April.) 855

XLVIII.—Address missing.—On the same subject. (13 April.) 858

XLIX.—Address missing.—That he cause the sentence of interdict pronounced by the Bishop of Huesca against the occupier of the church of Almodóvar to be firmly observed. (13 April.) 860

L.—To the master and brothers of the Order of the Temple established in Italy.—That preceptors of the Order of the Temple may act and defend in legal matters for their houses; neither their religious profession nor the fact that their origin is unknown is an impediment. (10 April.) 860

LI.—Address missing.—That he absolve the Bishop of Toul from excommunication. (18 April.) 861

LII.—To the Patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See, and the canons of the Lord’s Sepulchre.—A time-limit is granted for their appearance before the Apostolic presence concerning the archbishoprics of Tyre and Patras. (20 April.) 861

LIII.—To the Patriarch of Antioch.—The offence which he incurred by failing to visit the thresholds of the Apostles is remitted. (22 April.) 863

LIV.—To the Bishop of Ferrara.—That J., advanced as far as the priesthood although he had not been baptized, now that he has been baptized, be advanced to orders and the priesthood. (13 April.) 864

LV.—To the Archdeacon and penitentiary of Saint Victor’s, Paris, and Master R. de Corzon, canon of Noyon.—That they proceed under a specified form toward the absolution of the Bishop of Toul. (14 February.) 864

LVI.—To the Bishop of Maurienne, the Provost of Oulx, and the Dean of Helton, in the dioceses of Turin and Maurienne.—That they relinquish the fief of Javen to the monastery of Chiusa. (29 March.) 866

LVII.—To the Archbishop and Archdeacon of Sens.—That they admonish the Bishop and canons of Langres to assign to T., canon of Langres, the prebend which G., formerly Bishop of Langres, had assigned to him by papal command. (19 April.) 868

LVIII.—To the Abbot and convent of Cupro, of the Cistercian Order.—Certain goods given to them are confirmed. (12 April.) 869

LIX.—To the Bishops of Lübeck, Ratzeburg, and Schwerin.—That they impose, as a precaution, penance on a priest while he was sitting unaware when a sick boy died. (2 May.) 870

LX.—To the Archbishop of Salzburg, the Abbot of the diocese of Salzburg, and the Dean of Gurk.—He commits to them the case concerning the marriage of the King of Bohemia, up to the rendering of definitive judgment; he orders that, when they have been sufficiently instructed, they refer it for his examination. (26 April.) 871

LXI.—To the Count of Nevers and his wife.—They are granted that those who knew they were related in the fourth degree of consanguinity and did not say so when the marriage was contracted shall not be heard if they wish to accuse them. 872

LXII.—To the Prior and convent of Durham.—A religious may, through zeal for a holier life, transfer to a stricter religious order after first seeking, though not obtaining, permission from his prelate, even if the first monastery has such a privilege that transfer from it to another, even a stricter one, is impossible. (29 April.) 873

LXIII.—To the Archbishop of Pisa.—That he absolve the judge of Cagliari from his oath. (6 May.) 874

LXIV.—To the Dean and chapter of Stendal.—Certain goods are confirmed. (6 May.) 875

LXV.—To the Bishop of Vercelli.—That he accept the offering made by the sister of the Count of Montferrat of the castle of Montebello to the monastery of Rocca, where she established for the Roman Church an annual payment of forty pounds. (9 May.) 882

LXVI.—To the Abbot of Cîteaux, P. de Châteauneuf, and Brother R., legates of the Apostolic See.—He orders them not to harass the Archbishop of Narbonne on account of the crimes of which he had been convicted, since he has already granted him a time for performing penance. (9 May.) 882

LXVII.—To the Abbot of Saint Rufus and his brothers, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.—They are received under the protection of blessed Peter. (6 May.) 883

LXVIII.—To Helena, lady of Gallura.—The Pope’s cousin is sent to consummate marriage with her. (11 May.) 885

[Col. 1643]

LXIX.—To the Dean and subdean of Poitiers and the Dean of Asianus in the diocese of Poitiers.—He declares null the letters which C. Rufus had surreptitiously obtained concerning his claims against the chapter of Saintes. (9 May.) 888

LXX.—To the Bishop of Halberstadt.—In answer to an inquiry, it is stated that the first marriage, when another has followed, remains valid in a specified manner. (10 May.) 889

LXXI.—To the nobleman R., Count of Fondi.—That he will approve the agreement which he makes with the people of Terracina. (30 May.) 890

LXXII.—To the Bishop of Vercelli.—That he declare void letters obtained concerning matters belonging to the secular forum. (31 May.) 891

LXXIII.—To the Chapter of Saint Aredius.—That they confer the deanery of that church upon P., a clerk. (7 June.) 892

LXXIV.—To the illustrious King of Hungary.—That, if his wife’s brother possesses suitable learning and age, he will, at the king’s request, confirm him as Archbishop of Kalocsa. (7 June.) 892

LXXV.—To the Archbishop of Esztergom and the Bishop of Eger.—That they grant a dispensation in the marriage contracted between the Count Palatine and his wife. (7 June.) 893

LXXVI.—To the archbishops, bishops, and other prelates and princes of churches throughout Hungary.—That they cause an oath of fidelity to be made to the offspring of the King of Hungary. (7 June.) 894

LXXVII.—To the archbishops, bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches to whom these letters shall come.—That they absolve certain Templars returning from the pathless way to the way. (3 June.) 895

LXXVIII.—To the Bishop and clergy of Piacenza.—That the Pope is prepared to receive an oath from the consuls of Piacenza concerning devotion to the Church. (10 June.) 895

LXXIX.—To B., Archbishop of Torres.—That he inquire whether H. and the daughter of the Judge of Arborea are related in the fifth degree. (9 June.) 896

LXXX.—To J., cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he inquire into the condition of the priory of Bomin. (11 June.) 897

LXXXI.—To Angela, foundress, and the brothers of the church of Saint Mary of Monte di Guardia.—They are received under the protection of blessed Peter. (10 June.) 897

LXXXII.—To the clergy and people of Alessandria.—Concerning the union of the Churches of Alessandria and Acqui. (8 June.) 898

LXXXIII.—To the clergy and people of Acqui.—On the same subject. (8 June.) 898

LXXXIV.—To the Prior of Saint Andrew’s and his brothers.—They are received under the protection of blessed Peter. 901

LXXXV.—To the Abbot and chapter of the church of Dinant, in the diocese of Liège.—That they confer a benefice upon D., a clerk. (6 June.) 901

LXXXVI.—To the Bishop, Dean, and Chancellor of London.—That they not allow E., a woman, to be harassed. (13 June.) 901

LXXXVII.—To the Prior and convent of Saint Portianus in the diocese of Clermont.—That they no longer delay conferring the church of Bajec upon Durand, a clerk. (9 June.) 902

LXXXVIII.—To the Bishop of Clermont, the Abbot of Mozac, and Master Simon, archpriest of Hermenco, in the diocese of Clermont.—He orders them to cause to be observed what he has judicially decided in the case between the Prior of Montferrand and the procurator of the Hospitallers in the diocese of Clermont. (12 June.) 902

LXXXIX.—To B., Bishop of Pavia, and his successors canonically appointed.—The privileges and statutes of his church are confirmed. (12 June.) 903

XC.—To the Chapter of Como.—That they receive B., the Pope’s subdeacon, as a canon. (14 June.) 905

XCI.—To the Bishop of Pamplona, P. de Châteauneuf, and Brother
To the monks of Montfroid, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they hear the case in the matrimonial suit between the king of Aragon and M., daughter of G. of Montpellier. (15 Kalends of July.) 908

XCII.—To the chapter of Aix.—All the churches belonging to them are confirmed. (16 Kalends of July.) 909

XCIII.—Letter of the archpriest of Milan and the viscount.—How they carried out the commission entrusted to them for making peace between the cities of Alexandria and Acqui. 909

XCIV.—To P., podestà, and to the people of Alexandria.—On the same matter. (11 Kalends of July.) 911

[Col. 1644] XCV.—To all the clergy of Alexandria.—On the same matter. (11 Kalends of July.) 911

XCVI.—To Adolph, formerly archbishop of Cologne.—That he cease doing evil and return to the Church. (9 Kalends of July.) 911

XCVII.—To Albert, provost, elected archbishop of Magdeburg.—That he treat the apostolic messenger kindly. (11 Kalends of July.) 913

XCVIII.—To B., bishop of Pavia.—The monastery of Saint Mary and Saint Bartholomew is committed to his administration. (13 Kalends of July.) 913

XCIX.—To the bishop of Sabina.—He is restored to the same position for defending the rights of the Church which his predecessor held. (5 Kalends of July.) 914

C.—To P., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, and B., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they admonish the patriarch of Constantinople not to receive Venetians as canons of Saint Sophia, but others, provided that they are worthy men. (11 Kalends of July.) 914

CI.—To P., illustrious king of Aragon.—That the kings of Aragon may be crowned by the archbishop of Tarragona. 915

CII.—To the same.—That the goods of heretics whom he expels may be for his own use. (5 Ides of June.) 915

CIII.—To P. of Castelnau and the monks of Fontfroid, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they assign the castle of Scura to the king of Aragon for the extirpation of heretics. (5 Ides of June.) 916

CIV.—To the bishop of Auxerre.—That he decide concerning a certain marriage of the woman O. (5 Nones of July.) 916

CV.—To the provost and chapter of Saint Peter of Ronais.—That they receive the clerk Walter as a canon. (2 Ides of June.) 918

CVI.—To M., abbess of the monastery of Saints Innocent and Anastasius at Gandersheim, and to her sisters regularly appointed in perpetuity.—They are received under protection. (10 Kalends of July.) 919

CVII.—To the abbots of Helwatheshusen and Herwetheshusen, and to the dean of Paderborn.—It is declared that, in prescription of one hundred years against the Roman Church, the periods of schism are to be counted. (15 Kalends of July.) 921

CVIII.—To the same.—That they proceed in a specified manner concerning the adjudication of the subjection of the monastery of Gandersheim to the Church of Hildesheim. (15 Kalends of July.) 922

CIX.—To the bishop of Piacenza.—That, in the pending suit between the people of Ravenna and those of Faenza, he receive a specified number of witnesses. (10 Kalends of July.) 924

CX.—To W., bishop of Nevers, and H., archdeacon of Bourges.—He commits to them the case of W., a burgess of La Charité, suspected of heresy. (Kalends of June.) 926

CXI.—To the bishop, Master Guido, archdeacon of Limoges, and the abbot of Bule, in the diocese of Limoges.—He commits to them the suit pending between the abbot and convent of Mauzac on the one side and the Templars of Tourette on the other, concerning the tithes of the lands of Sancolt. (Kalends of July.) 928

CXII.—To Hugh, canon of Saint Genoult of Toul; W., canon of the church of Liverdun; and Lambert, canon of Lincien in the diocese of Toul.—He commits to them the suit pending between the priest G. on one side and the abbot of Saint Leo of Toul on the other, concerning the despoiling of the benefice of Nais. (7 Ides of July.) 930

CXIII.—To the bishop of Cenad and the abbot of Cikedor.—That they protect and defend the bishop of Pécs, falsely accused of a crime. (Nones of July.) 931

CXIV.—To the bishop of Como.—That he recover his possessions unlawfully alienated. (5 Ides of July.) 934

CXV.—To Odo, abbot of the monastery of Saint Vaast of Arras, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.—The goods and statutes of the said monastery are confirmed. (6 Kalends of July.) 934

CXVI.—To the abbot and chapter of Saint Vaast of Arras.—On the same matter. (6 Kalends of July.) 938

CXVII.—To the provost and chapter of Lens.—That they provide the clerk P. with a benefice. (Ides of June.) 939

CXVIII.—To the abbot of Saint Bartholomew, and Gosbert and Drogo of Cordolio, canons of Noyon.—That they cause the clerk S. to enjoy peaceful possession of the church of Fraitoi. (3 Ides of July.) 939

CXIX.—To all abbots assembled in the general Cistercian chapter.—That they pray for him. (5 Ides of July.) 940

CXX.—To the cellarer, M. Asinus, and R., canons of Speyer.—That they cause a judgment rendered by their fellow canons concerning a certain election, if it is just, to be observed. (2 Ides of July.) 942

CXXI.—To the master and brethren of the hospital of Neufchâtel-de-Driencourt.—Their goods are received under protection. (17 Kalends of August.) 944

CXXII.—To the dean and chapter of Laon.—Confirmation of the statutes of the Church of Laon. 944

CXXIII.—To the bishop of Laon.—That he confer prebends in the Church of Laon upon Master Alberic. (9 Kalends of August.) 944

CXXIV.—To the dean and chapter of Laon.—That, should controversies arise between the chapter and the bishop concerning the customs of the Church, the canons themselves may produce witnesses. (11 Kalends of August.) 945

CXXV.—To the bishop of Saragossa.—That he abolish a statute providing that no one may be received as a canon unless all the canons consent; or that “all” be understood to mean the greater part. (11 Kalends of August.) 945

CXXVI.—To Walter, clerk, provost of the church of Saint Mary, called in Greek *Ypanimnitos* and in Latin *Misericordia* (“Mercy”), belonging to the illustrious Emperor B. of Constantinople.—His provostship is confirmed. (10 Kalends of August.) 946

CXXVII.—To Lambert, priest, chaplain of the illustrious Emperor B. of Constantinople, provost of Saint Michael at Constantinople.—A like confirmation is made. (10 Kalends of August.) 946

CXXVIII.—To Absalon, priest.—The provostship in the church of Blessed Mary of Scota near Constantinople, as he possesses it justly and peaceably, is confirmed to him by apostolic authority. (10 Kalends of August.) 946

CXXIX.—To Walter of Courtrai.—His institution is confirmed. (8 Kalends of August.) 946

CXXX.—To the patriarch of Constantinople.—That he is not bound to observe the oath made by him with the Venetians, that he would receive no one as a canon of Saint Sophia unless he were a Venetian. (11 Kalends of July.) 947

CXXXI.—No address.—Reprisals are granted against the goods of the hostile people of Piacenza. (7 Kalends of August.) 948

CXXXII.—To the archbishop of Reims, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, legate of the Apostolic See, and to his suffragans.—He orders the observance of the sentence of excommunication which the bishop of Cambrai had pronounced against certain criminal citizens of Cambrai. (3 Ides of July.) 949

CXXXIII.—To Clement, provost of Saint Stephen at Constantinople.—His provostship is confirmed. (5 Kalends of August.) 951

CXXXIV.—To Master Clement, canon of Saint Sophia at Constantinople.—On a similar matter. (5 Kalends of August.) 951

CXXXV.—To the archbishop of Bari and the bishop of Salpi.—That they hear and determine the case between the archbishops of Trani and Acerenza. (6 Kalends of August.) 951

CXXXVI.—To Brother Augustine, regular canon of the church of Saint Mary of Norton.—That he retain the name given him, not at baptism but upon profession. (3 Kalends of August.) 955

CXXXVII.—To the bishop, archpriest, and chapter of Padua.—That they receive the clerk C. as a canon. (2 Nones of August.) 955

CXXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Tyre.—That he send to the court his proofs concerning the church of Saint Mark near Tyre, which the Venetians complain has been occupied. (3 Nones of August.) 956

CXXXIX.—To the noble duke and the people of Venice.—They are rebuked for the invasion of Zadar and exhorted to be devout. (Nones of August.) 957

CXL.—To T., patriarch of Constantinople.—An answer is given concerning certain articles relating to the state of the Church of Constantinople. (4 Nones of August.) 957

CXLI.—To the archbishop of Nicosia.—That he present himself before the apostolic presence. (Nones of August.) 966

CXLII.—To T., patriarch of Constantinople.—The agreement made between him and the governor of the empire of Constantinople is ordered to be observed. (Nones of August.) 967

CXLIII.—To R., bishop of Saragossa.—The abbot of Pina is condemned to pay tithes and provide procuration for him. (2 Nones of August.) 969

CXLIV.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Pontianus of Lucca.—That they are not bound to receive J., removed from the monastery because of an offence. (4 Nones of August.) 972

CXLV.—To the abbot of Saint Eugenius, the parish priest of Saint Peter in Pisside, and Boniface, canon of the parish church of Marculfo, in the dioceses of Siena and Florence.—That they cause the sentence of excommunication pronounced by the bishop of Volterra to be observed. (5 Ides of August.) 973

CXLVI.—To the archbishop of Torres.—That he absolve the Church of Thergo from payment of census, if he finds it exempt. (5 Ides of August.) 975

[Col. 1646] CXLVII.—To the archbishops and bishops established throughout Sardinia.—That, in accordance with promise and oath, they compel the lady of Gallura to contract marriage with the pope’s cousin. 975

CXLVIII.—To the patriarch and chapter of Constantinople.—That they receive the clerk C. as a canon of the church of Saint Sophia. (7 Kalends of September.) 975

CXLIX.—To the abbot and convent of Fossanova.—The agreement between them and the people of Piperno is confirmed. (5 Kalends of September.) 976

CL.—To the clergy of Barcelona.—That the sacrament of faith is not to be denied to either Saracen or Jew who requests it. (7 Kalends of September.) 977

CLI.—To the bishop of Penne.—That he compel the clerics of Saint Serotinus to allow the inhabitants of the castle of Loreto to receive chrism in the church of Saint Peter in that castle. (8 Ides of September.) 979

CLII.—To the bishop and chapter of Pamplona.—That they receive the clerk H. as a canon. (13 Kalends of September.) 979

CLIII.—To the abbot of Saint Victor, the archdeacon, and the dean of Saint German of Auxerre, at Paris.—He commits to them the suit pending between the deacon G. and F. of Canduerre, in the diocese of Noyon, concerning a certain tithe. (7 Ides of September.) 980

CLIV.—To the abbot and brethren of the monastery of Fossanova.—The agreement made between them and the people of Piperno is confirmed. (3 Nones of September.) 982

CLV.—To the bishop of Veroli.—That he restrain the inhabitants of the castle of Frosinone who are occupying the goods of the church. (4 Kalends of August.) 983

CLVI.—To the cantor, Fulk of Saint Remigius, and Master Adam, canons of Reims.—That they cause the priest H. to be provided for by the bishop of Arras. (2 Ides of September.) 984

CLVII.—To the king of Sicily.—He rejoices at his beneficial advancement and exhorts him to persevere in virtue. 984

CLVIII.—To Arcadius and all the people of Gaeta, Antella, Platana, Jaci, and Celsus, and to all Gaetans and Saracens established throughout Sicily: may they understand and love the truth, which is God.—He commends them for their fidelity and steadfastness toward the king of Sicily. 985

CLIX.—To the venerable brother, bishop of Metz.—He answers various questions and inquiries. (5 Kalends of September.) 985

CLX.—To the archbishop of Tarragona, the abbot of Saint Mary of Poblet in the diocese of Tarragona, and the archdeacon of Barcelona.—That they proceed against the bishop of Vic if ill repute has preceded. (Kalends of September.) 988

CLXI.—To the podestà and people of Spoleto.—That they do not presume to appoint judges to the prejudice of the pope. (12 Kalends of October.) 989

CLXII.—To B., archpriest of the parish church of Bertinoro.—He is received under protection. (7 Kalends of October.) 989

CLXIII.—To the provost, dean, and chapter of Constance.—The election of the bishop of Constance is confirmed, and administration of the Church of Constance is granted to him. (2 Kalends of October.) 990

CLXIV.—To the archdeacon of Paris and Master R. of Courson, canon of Noyon.—He commits to them the case of the election of the abbot of Saint Martin of Troyes. (6 Nones of October.) 991

CLXV.—To the dean and chapter of Saint Martin of Tours.—That they receive Master J. of Cangé as canon and brother. (3 Nones of October.) 994

CLXVI.—To all the archbishops and bishops of Lombardy.—That, if the citizens of Piacenza do not desist from oppressing the Church of Piacenza, they be deprived of their episcopal see. (7 Ides of October.) 995

CLXVII.—To the podestà, consuls, and people of Piacenza: the spirit of wiser counsel.—On the same matter. (Nones of October.) 998

CLXVIII.—To the bishop of Vercelli, the abbot of Tiglieto, and Albert, priest of Mantua. (Nones of October.) 1000

CLXIX.—To the consuls of Piacenza: the spirit of wiser counsel.—He rejoices that, returned to devotion, they have ceased from offences against the Church and obey apostolic commands. 1001

CLXX.—To the prior and convent of Saint Vincent of Lisbon.—A certain agreement made between them and the bishop and chapter of Lisbon is confirmed. (17 Kalends of November.) 1001

CLXXI.—To the bishop of Florence.—Concerning the ordination of certain canons in the Church of Volterra. (16 Kalends of November.) 1002

CLXXII.—To P., bishop of Ivrea.—That he return to his Church and not seek separation from it. (12 Kalends of November.) 1004

[Col. 1647] CLXXIII.—To the bishop of Zamora, etc.—He writes to them in favor of the monastery of Lorvão against the king of Portugal. 1008

CLXXIV.—To the provost of Novara.—That he not permit the clerk A. to be harassed concerning his benefice on account of a wound inflicted by him upon a certain robber. (2 Kalends of November.) 1008

CLXXV.—To archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established throughout Poland.—That they give counsel and support to the abbot of Łękno, who is preaching the faith. (7 Kalends of November.) 1009

CLXXVI.—To the dean and chapter of Lincoln.—That they elect a worthy person as their bishop. (2 Kalends of November.) 1011

CLXXVII.—To the abbot and convent of Salem.—That it be lawful for them to lend money to their persecutors. (2 Nones of November.) 1012

CLXXVIII.—To the bishop of Ferrara.—That he induce the clergy and people of Trent to obey the patriarch of Aquileia, to whom administration of the Church of Trent has been committed because of their scandal. (2 Kalends of November.) 1013

CLXXIX.—To the master and brethren of the lepers of Vaisliac.—All the goods which they hold are confirmed. (9 Kalends of October.) 1019

CLXXX.—To the master and brethren of the militia of the Temple beyond the sea.—The grant of Satalia made to them by the Venetians is confirmed. (2 Kalends of November.) 1019

CLXXXI.—To the podestà, consuls, and citizens of Ferrara.—That they return to devotion to the Church and make satisfaction to the abbot of Pomposa for the attack. (5 Ides of November.) 1020

CLXXXII.—To the bishop and chapter of Maurienne.—That they receive Master Ph. as canon and brother. (2 Nones of November.) 1021

CLXXXIII.—No address.—On the same matter. (2 Nones of November.) 1022

CLXXXIV.—To the abbot of Saint Aubert, the dean, and Master R. of Bekerel, canon of Cambrai.—That they cause a prebend to be assigned to R. of Vaisliac by the bishop and chapter of Soissons, according to the tenor of apostolic letters already issued on this matter. (13 Kalends of November.) 1022

CLXXXV.—To R., monk of Montfroid, legate of the Apostolic See.—That he appoint preachers against the heretics rising up in the province of Narbonne. (15 Kalends of December.) 1024

CLXXXVI.—To the prior and chapter of Gubbio.—The election which they made for bishop of Gubbio having been annulled, they are ordered to make another. (6 Kalends of December.) 1025

CLXXXVII.—To the bishop of Bamberg.—That he return to the king of Hungary and declare the joy conceived by the pope at the reception of his son. (3 Kalends of December.) 1028

CLXXXVIII.—To scholars residing at Vicenza.—He commends them for their devotion in constructing a certain church. 1028

CLXXXIX.—To the noble man B., marquis of Montferrat.—The pope’s goodwill is offered to him. (5 Kalends of December.) 1028

CXC.—To B., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, legate of the Apostolic See.—On the same matter. (5 Kalends of December.) 1029

CXCI.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—That he devote attention to negotiating peace between certain dissenting citizens. (5 Kalends of December.) 1030

CXCII.—To the bishop of Samaria.—The grant of Mount Saint is confirmed to him. (5 Kalends of December.) 1030

CXCIII.—To the clerics of the island of Negroponte.—They are received under protection. (5 Kalends of December.) 1030

CXCIV.—To the elect of Athens.—His institution is confirmed. (5 Kalends of December.) 1031

CXCV.—To the nobleman P., count of Celano, master justiciar of Apulia and the Terra di Lavoro: the spirit of wiser counsel.—He is reproved for obstinacy against the Church and admonished to return to it. (8 Ides of December.) 1031

CXCVI.—To Ralph, bishop of Arras.—He forbids anyone, without consultation with the Roman pontiff, to dare pronounce a sentence of excommunication against him. (14 Kalends of January.) 1034

CXCVII.—To the bishop of Soissons.—That he remit ecclesiastical censures to those who had entered tournaments, lest delay be caused to the holy expedition. (4 Ides of December.) 1035

CXCVIII.—To the bishop of Soissons, G., provost of Douai, brother of Henry, emperor of Constantinople, and the cantor of Paris.—If they take the journey by land, he promises them safe conduct as far as Brindisi. (4 Ides of December.) 1036

CXCIX.—To the counts, barons, knights, and all the crusaders.—He urges them to bring aid to Emperor Henry. (3 Ides of December.) 1036

[Col. 1648] CC.—To the bishop of Soissons.—He grants him permission to accept the Church of Thessalonica while retaining the Church of Soissons. (4 Ides of December.) 1037

CCI.—To the people of Sutri.—That they not choose a stranger to govern their city without consulting the pope. 1038

CCII.—To the prior and canons of Saint Paternianus in the diocese of Foligno.—That the subjection of the church of Saint Christina be adjudged to them. (Nones of December.) 1038

CCIII.—To the archbishop of Toledo.—That he impose salutary penance upon the priest G., who, through simplicity, had sung a psalm in place of the canon of the Mass. (17 Kalends of January.) 1042

CCIV.—To the podestà, consuls, and council of Faenza.—That they expel from their territories the poor men of Lyon and other heretics. (2 Ides of December.) 1042

CCV.—To the prior and convent of Canterbury.—They are absolved from the claim of their suffragans concerning the right of electing an archbishop. (13 Kalends of January.) 1043

CCVI.—To the illustrious king of England.—On the same matter. 1044

CCVII.—To the prior and convent of Canterbury.—On the same subject. (12 Kalends of January.) 1048

CCVIII.—To the abbots of Saint Méen and Montfort, and R., archdeacon of Saint-Malo.—That they proceed against schisms and perverse opinions. (12 Kalends of January.) 1049

CCIX.—To the archbishop of Bordeaux and the abbot of La Sauve-Majeure in the diocese of Bordeaux.—That they determine what is canonical against Hugh Brun, who had presumed to remove from the monastery of Obazine a virgin betrothed to God and take her as his wife. (13 Kalends of January.) 1051

CCX.—To the abbot of Evesham, the prior of Wychilicumb, and the prior of Evesham, in the diocese of Worcester.—That they not proceed, in the case concerning the patronage of the church of Filebi, on the pretext of letters falsely obtained. (3 Nones of January.) 1051

CCXI.—To the abbot and convent of Fossanova.—The judgment rendered in their favor concerning a certain possession against A., a Saracen, is confirmed. (5 Ides of January.) 1053

CCXII.—To the bishop of Spoleto.—That he not harass the rectors of the parish district of Saint Fortunatus. (3 Ides of January.) 1056

CCXIII.—To the abbot and monks of Saint Hippolytus of Faenza.—That they cause the body of a heretic to be disinterred. (5 Ides of January.) 1057

CCXIV.—To the archbishop, dean, and chapter of Magdeburg.—That they receive O., who has been emancipated, as a canon. (6 Ides of January.) 1058

CCXV.—To the dean and chapter of Magdeburg.—That they confer the provostship upon O., nephew of the duke of Poland. (6 Ides of January.) 1059

CCXVI.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—That he absolve Duke Wladislaus. (2 Ides of January.) 1059

CCXVII.—To the nobleman Duke Wladislaus: the spirit of wiser counsel.—He is reproved for his obstinacy and perpetration of evils, and exhorted to repentance. (2 Nones of January.) 1060

CCXVIII.—To all bishops of Poland.—On the same matter. (4 Ides of January.) 1062

CCXIX.—To all Christ’s faithful established in Poland.—That they pay the due census to the Roman Church. (Nones of January.) 1063

CCXX.—To all dukes established in Poland.—That they not impede payment of tithes. (2 Nones of January.) 1063

CCXXI.—To the chaplains of the duke and of the other nobles of Poland.—That they pay cathedraticum. (2 Nones of January.) 1064

CCXXII.—To all clerics holding ecclesiastical benefices in Poland.—That they give unanimous support to the archbishop of Gniezno. (2 Nones of January.) 1064

CCXXIII.—To all dukes established in Poland.—That they permit elections of churches to be freely celebrated by the chapters. (2 Nones of January.) 1064

CCXXIV.—To the chapter of the church of Łęczyca.—He confirms to them, as they possess it, a certain prebend. (2 Nones of January.) 1065

CCXXV.—To the same.—A similar grant concerning the chantry. (2 Nones of January.) 1065

CCXXVI.—To the cantor of the church of Gniezno.—A similar grant concerning the chapel. (2 Nones of January.) 1065

CCXXVII.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—He gives him authority to exercise canonical censure against Duke Wladislaus and his supporters unless he repents. (4 Ides of January.) 1066

CCXXVIII.—To all bishops established in Poland.—That they cause the sentence rendered against the bishop of Poznań to be observed. (4 Ides of January.) 1066

[Col. 1649] CCXXIX.—To the duke of Cracow.—He is received under protection. (2 Nones of January.) 1067

CCXXX.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—That he restrain laymen despoiling clerics. (2 Nones of January.) 1067

CCXXXI.—To the bishop of Pomerania.—That he obey the archbishop of Gniezno. (Nones of January.) 1068

CCXXXII.—To all bishops established in Poland.—That they assist the said archbishop. (Nones of January.) 1068

CCXXXIII.—To the chapter of the church of Łęczyca.—Their possessions and goods are confirmed, as they hold them justly. (7 Ides of January.) 1068

CCXXXIV.—To the archbishop of Poland.—That the benefices of his church may not be conferred by secular persons. (4 Ides of January.) 1069

CCXXXV.—To the archbishop of Gniezno and his suffragans.—That they not admit publicly married men to ecclesiastical dignities. (6 Ides of January.) 1070

CCXXXVI.—To the noblemen, dukes established in Poland.—That they desist from occupying the resources of vacant churches. (4 Ides of January.) 1071

CCXXXVII.—To the provost and chapter of Harlebeche.—That they receive the clerk P. as a canon. (4 Ides of January.) 1072

CCXXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—That he may carry the sign of the cross throughout his province. (2 Ides of January.) 1073

CCXXXIX.—To the same.—That he compel the canons of Saint Albert and Saint Peter to pay the census. 1073

CCXL.—To the prior and brethren of Kening.—They are received under the protection of Saint Peter. (17 Kalends of February.) 1073

CCXLI.—To the archbishop of Gniezno.—That, should he happen to die first, his successor be bound for his debts. 1074

CCXLII.—To Garin, abbot, and the monks of the monastery of Saint Aper of Toul, present and future, professing the regular life in perpetuity.—They are received under the protection of Blessed Peter. (3 Ides of February.) 1074

CCXLIII.—To the patriarch of Constantinople.—The sentence rendered against Venetians entering his church violently in order to seize Ivona is confirmed. (Ides of January.) 1077

CCXLIV.—To the elect and chapter of the church of Modon.—They are received under protection. (14 Kalends of February.) 1079

CCXLV.—To the same.—Their statute concerning tithes is confirmed. (14 Kalends of February.) 1079

CCXLVI.—To the same.—That they apply the revenues of a vacant prebend to common uses. (14 Kalends of February.) 1079

CCXLVII.—To the chaplain of the church of Saint Nicholas of Modon outside the port.—The income of forty *hyperpyra* assigned to him by the prince of Achaea is confirmed by apostolic authority. (14 Kalends of February.) 1079

CCXLVIII.—To the bishop of Pamplona, P. of Castelnau, and Brother Rad., monk of Fontfroid, legates of the Apostolic See.—That they proceed, according to the previous mandate, in the case concerning the king’s marriage. (5 Kalends of February.) 1080

CCXLIX.—To the illustrious king of Sicily.—He rejoices that he has been freed from the custody of unworthy persons and exhorts him to do good. (4 Kalends of February.) 1081

CCL.—To the household officers of the king of Sicily.—On the same matter. 1082

CCLI.—To archbishops and prelates, and to counts, throughout the kingdom of Sicily.—That they obey and support the king of Sicily. 1082

CCLII.—To the bishop of Soissons.—That he annul actions undertaken against the goods of his church. (4 Kalends of February.) 1082

CCLIII.—To the patriarch of Jerusalem, legate of the Apostolic See.—The deadline for coming to the Roman court is extended. (3 Nones of February.) 1083

CCLIV.—To the same.—An answer is given to his inquiry concerning points requiring clarification. (2 Kalends of February.) 1083

CCLV.—To the bishop of Ely.—That he absolve the subdeacon P. from his vow. (7 Ides of February.) 1085

CCLVI.—To the bishop of Florence.—That he promote the deacon F. to sacred orders. (8 Ides of February.) 1085

CCLVII.—To the chapter of Vaste.—A certain arrangement made in its church by the chapter is tolerated. (7 Ides of February.) 1086

CCLVIII.—To R., bishop, and the clergy of Viterbo.—That they restore what J. had lost because of his defence of the faith, having been taken away by the Patarenes. (Nones of February.) 1086

CCLIX.—To the bishops of Chalon and Châlons, and the prior of Clairvaux.—He commits to them for determination the case of the bishop of Toul. (Kalends of February.) 1087

CCLX.—To the bishops of Langres and Châlons, and the prior of Clairvaux.—He commits to them the case concerning the primicery of Toul. (Kalends of February.) 1090

CCLXI.—To the chapter and all the clergy of Magdeburg.—The election of an archbishop is confirmed. (6 Ides of February.) 1093

CCLXII.—To the provost and canons of Saint Mary of Magdeburg.—The hospital of Saint Alexius is confirmed. (6 Ides of February.) 1094

CCLXIII.—To the same.—The privileges granted to them by Roman pontiffs are confirmed. (5 Ides of February.) 1095

CCLXIV.—To the provost, cantor, and master of schools of Reims.—That they compel the bishop of Tournai to provide for the subdeacon J. according to the tenor of the apostolic mandate already issued on this matter. (3 Nones of January.) 1096

CCLXV.—To the bishop of Langres.—He answers concerning the privileges of the chapel of the duke of Dijon. (14 Kalends of March.) 1097

CCLXVI.—To the bishop, dean, and chapter of Langres.—That they receive Hugh of Faverney as a canon and brother. (12 Kalends of March.) 1098

CCLXVII.—To the bishop, abbot of Saint Martin, and cantor of Limoges.—That they subject to excommunication those who have invaded the goods of P., subdeacon and papal notary. (12 Kalends of March.) 1098

CCLXVIII.—To Albert, archbishop of Magdeburg.—That he invalidate certain grants of benefices made contrary to right. (Ides of February.) 1100

CCLXIX.—To the same.—The establishment of certain churches is confirmed. (14 Kalends of March.) 1101

CCLXX.—To the abbot of Sichen in the diocese of Halberstadt, the scholastic of Saint Sebastian, and Master Arnold, parish priest of Saint John of Magdeburg.—That they investigate the offences of the provost of Hunoldesburg and report. (13 Kalends of March.) 1101

CCLXXI.—To the bishop and chapter of Limoges.—That they receive R. of Tours as a canon and brother. (11 Kalends of March.) 1102

## Book Ten

In the tenth year of the pontificate, A.D. 1207.

I.—To the abbot of Evesham.—He remits to him his excommunicated monk A., that he may dispense with him concerning certain matters. (2 Kalends of March.) 1103

II.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Vaast of Arras.—The privilege of Pope Alexander, concerning the prohibition against granting certain prebends received by the canons of Saint Peter, is confirmed to them. (5 Kalends of March.) 1104

III.—To the same.—A certain proceeding is annulled and certain indulgences are confirmed. (4 Kalends of March.) 1105

IV.—To the abbot of Saint Aubert, the cantor, and Master R. of Bekerel, canon of Cambrai.—That they cause the subdeacon Hugh to be received to the vacant canonry and prebend of the church of Bruges. 1105

V.—To the nobleman B., duke of Saxony.—He and his goods are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (5 Nones of March.) 1106

VI.—To Sophia, abbess of the monastery of Quedlinburg, and her sisters, present and future, regularly substituted in perpetuity.—The monastery itself is made immediately subject to the Roman pontiff, and certain other concessions are made to them, always saving the annual census of one pound of silver. (Nones of March.) 1106

VII.—To the chapter of Magdeburg.—They are forbidden to sell or lease certain of their rights and goods to persons other than canons. (2 Nones of March.) 1108

VIII.—To the bishops of Halberstadt and Merseburg, and the abbot of Saint John on the Mount at Magdeburg.—That they not refuse to receive priests and other suitable men into that church as canons and brethren, notwithstanding a privilege once granted to them. (8 Ides of March.) 1108

IX.—To Master Gervand.—The conferment upon him of a certain prebend at Magdeburg is confirmed. (6 Ides of March.) 1109

X.—To the chapter of Magdeburg.—On the same matter; and for the same G. it is written that they receive and admit him. 1110

XI.—To Albert, archbishop of Magdeburg.—On the same matter and for the same G. 1110

XII.—To the bishop of Merseburg and the elect of Brandenburg and Havelberg.—On the same matter. 1110

XIII.—To the clerk Ulric.—The custody of Saint Peter at Liège, conferred upon him, is confirmed. (6 Nones of March.) 1110

XIV.—To Luke, abbot, and the convent of Bourgueil.—A definite manner of living and governing the monastery is prescribed, following the report of certain persons to whom its correction had been entrusted. (7 Ides of March.) 1111

XV.—To the bishop and dean of Paris.—That they proceed against certain forgers, punishing them by the penalty enacted against forgers. (5 Ides of March.) 1113

[Col. 1651] XVI.—To Elias, abbot, and the convent of Radingia of the Cluniac order.—The monastery itself and their goods are received under protection, and their privileges are confirmed. (4 Kalends of March.) 1115

XVII.—To the same.—Permission is granted them to recover alienated goods of the monastery. 1115

XVIII.—To the abbot of Radingia.—That, in the external administrations of the monastery, he may freely appoint and remove brethren proved in religious profession as he sees fit. (6 Ides of March.) 1115

XIX.—To the dean major, priors, and other clerics of Cologne.—Afflicted by adverse tribulations, they are comforted and encouraged to be stronger and fearless. (3 Ides of March.) 1116

XX.—To the archbishop of Tours and the abbots of Chaloceio and Oratory, of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Angers.—That they induce and compel Hilary, abbot of Bourgueil, to go to the monastery of Saint Jovinus, in order to perform there the fruitful penance imposed upon him. (16 Kalends of April.) 1118

XXI.—To the abbot and convent of Bourgueil.—They are ordered and permitted to revoke the grants and pensions unlawfully made by Hilary, formerly their abbot. 1119

XXII.—To the archbishop of Tours and the abbots of Oratory and Chaloceio, of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Angers.—That they cause full justice to be rendered to those complaining of debts legitimately contracted in the time of Hilary, formerly abbot of Bourgueil.

XXIII.—To the archbishop of Tours and the bishops of Poitiers and Angers.—That they proceed against the incendiaries of a certain grange of Hilary, formerly abbot of Bourgueil. (12 Kalends of April.) 1120

XXIV.—To the abbot and convent of Bourgueil.—That they punish certain monks of the said monastery, accomplices of Hilary, formerly abbot of that monastery, and summon them to obedience, and not permit them to disturb the monastery. (16 Kalends of April.) 1121

XXV.—To the abbots of Marmoutier, Saint Julian, and Saint Florentius, in the dioceses of Tours and Angers.—That they compel Hilary, formerly abbot of Bourgueil, to return to the cloister assigned to him for doing penance. (14 Kalends of April.) 1121

XXVI.—To the archbishop of Tours, the bishop of Angers, and the abbot of Oratory of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Angers.—On the same matter, as above. 1122

XXVII.—To Matthew, provost, and
To the canons of the church of Blessed Lawrence of Jovisville, present and future, in perpetuity.—They are received under the protection of the Apostolic See, together with all their goods, liberties, immunities, and privileges. (11 Kalends of April.) 1122

XXVIII.—To Elias, abbot of Radingia, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—They are received under protection, etc., as above, together with certain other alms granted in favour of religion. (10 Kalends of April.) 1123

XXIX.—To the nobleman M. of Romania.—A decision is made concerning the restoration of the right of patronage of the church of Saint Angelus of Casaperota. (9 Kalends of April.) 1125

XXX.—To the podestà and people of Faenza.—A truce is granted concerning the dispute which they have with the Church of Ravenna. 1126

XXXI.—To the bishop … and H., abbot of Aberbruhot, Th., prior, Ralph, archdeacon, and Master Lawrence, official of Saint Andrew.—They are commissioned to settle certain disputes concerning certain tithes. (13 Kalends of April.) 1126

XXXII.—To the priors and brethren of Kirkeham, Guisborough, Bridlington, Newburgh, and others of the same order established in the diocese of York.—Authority is committed to them to reform and correct the churches subject to them. (16 Kalends of April.) 1128

XXXIII.—To the bishops of Monopoli, Polignano, and Conversano.—That they may confirm the election of Benedict, bishop of the island of Cephalonia, if he is suitable and the election has been canonically made. (10 Kalends of April.) 1129

XXXIV.—To the bishop, dean, and archdeacon of Noyon.—That they shall have the sentence pronounced and confirmed on behalf of Guiburge, a poor widow, carried into execution. (9 Kalends of April.) 1129

XXXV.—To the clergy and people of Verisien[ne].—That they shall render obedience and reverence to Master Garin, elected archbishop of Verisien[ne]. (3 Kalends of April.) 1130

XXXVI.—To G., archbishop of Verisien[ne].—It is decreed [Col. 1652] that sentences of excommunication and suspension pronounced without reasonable cause are not binding, and that a sentence issued after an appeal has been lodged is not to be observed, as being void. 1131

XXXVII.—To the same.—Permission is granted to retain the benefices which he held in that city before his promotion. 1131

XXXVIII.—To all Christ’s faithful signed with the cross and established in the regions of Romania.—They are urged to assist in the service of our Creator against the faithless, terrible, and powerful pagans. 1131

XXXIX.—To A., the illustrious king of Hungary.—A reply is made, urging him not to take it ill if the election, made to the archbishopric of Kalocsa, of the provost of Pabenburg, brother of his wife and a man then under age and otherwise unlearned, cannot be confirmed. (Nones of April.) 1132

XL.—To the abbot and convent of Cambuschineo, diocese of Saint Andrew.—It is decreed that, in confirming their privilege at the petition of the abbot and convent of Dunfermline, there was no intention to confer a new right, but to preserve that which had been conferred. (Nones of April.) 1134

XLI.—To the illustrious king of the Danes.—Thanks are given for the release of the bishop of Schleswig; and, the cause of the revenues imposed upon him having been advocated, the king is urged to allow that bishop to enjoy the fruits of his bishopric through his administrator. (4 Nones of April.) 1134

XLII.—To Philip, illustrious king of the Franks.—He is urged to treat I., his wife, with marital affection. 1135

XLIII.—To the bishops of Ely and Chichester.—That they shall persuade the justices of the kingdom of England, even by ecclesiastical censure, not to hinder the vows undertaken by pilgrims signed with the cross. (8 Ides of April.) 1136

XLIV.—To the archbishop …, the subdean of Saint Martin, and Master Socrates, canon of Tours.—The matrimonial cause of I. of Alcia and M., his wife, is entrusted to them for determination. 1137

XLV.—To the bishop of Saint Andrew.—Concerning the declaration of obedience and the exemption of parish churches, and concerning burials and certain other matters belonging to that bishop. (8 Ides of April.) 1138

XLVI.—To the marquis of Malaspina.—He is forbidden, on the pretext of a toll established before the Lateran Council, to presume to receive anything in his land except what he had previously received. (4 Ides of April.) 1140

XLVII.—To the archbishop of Ravenna.—Permission is granted him to receive and use the pallium. (16 Kalends of May.) 1140

XLVIII.—To the prior and brethren of Grandmont.—That they may pour out prayers for the soul of M., archbishop of Tours, so that he may be delivered from the penalties which he may perhaps have deserved for his transgressions. (5 Ides of April.) 1140

XLIX.—To bishops, abbots, priors, and all clerics established throughout Achaea.—That they may strive to assist the archbishop of Patras with charitable aid in paying his debts. (4 Kalends of May.) 1141

L.—To the archbishop of Patras.—That he shall not permit the clerics of his province to receive ecclesiastical revenues if they disdain personally to serve in the benefices, unless it is established to him that they were canonically promoted; and that he shall compel beneficed clerics to reside in their churches. 1142

LI.—To the same.—That he shall not permit those who come to the regions of Achaea to celebrate [the liturgy]. (13 Kalends of May.) 1142

LII.—To the bishop of Padua.—At the request of the patriarch of Aquileia, while the latter presided over the Church of Padua, he is commissioned concerning a notable site where he may erect a cathedral church in the place of Vienna. (18 Kalends of May.) 1143

LIII.—To the bishop …, the provost of Saint Lucius, and the scholasticus of Chur.—They are commissioned to ensure that H., a poor priest of the Church of Rapis, enjoys peaceful possession, as justice shall require. (14 Kalends of May.) 1145

LIV.—To the podestà and consuls, present and future, and to all the people of Treviso.—They are urged to acquiesce in and trust their bishop regarding the correction of the abominable and schismatic errors which they maintain against the faith; and that bishop is to correct the offences of the clerics. (11 Kalends of May.) 1146

LV.—To the bishop of Brixen, H., provost of Aquileia, and S., scholasticus of Augsburg.—The examination of witnesses is entrusted to them concerning the election of a pastor of the Church of Gurk, an election in respect of which the Church of Salzburg claimed a right. (14 Kalends of April.) 1148

LVI.—To the chapter of Patras.—That they shall receive the archbishop of Patras, elected in concord, as their true archbishop. (8 Kalends of May.) 1151

LVII.—To the archdeacon … and the provost of Setara, our subdeacon and canon of Milan.—That they shall hear and duly bring to conclusion the cause pending between C., a scholar, and John, a cleric. (5 Kalends of May.) 1152

LVIII.—To the bishops of Zamora, Segovia, and Ávila.—That if Master I., scholasticus of the Church of Palencia, proceeds maliciously against the bishop of Palencia by alleging crimes against him, he shall be suspended from office and benefice. (5 Ides of May.) 1154

LIX.—To the prioress and sisters of Sexen, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Privileges are granted to them, and their liberties and immunities are confirmed. (7 Ides of May.) 1155

LX.—To the canons of Saint Maurice of Augsburg, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.—Privileges and indulgences are granted, and their liberties, etc., are confirmed. (7 Ides of May.) 1156

LXI.—To the bishop of Auxerre.—Concerning the tithes of Jews, the revenues of scholars, and usurers. (17 Kalends of June.) 1157

LXII.—To the dean of the major church and the prior of Cologne.—Concerning beneficed persons who are excommunicated or under interdict, etc. (Ides of May.) 1158

LXIII.—To the archbishop of Pisa.—A matrimonial cause is committed to him. (17 Kalends of June.) 1159

LXIV.—To the consuls and people of Piacenza.—Concerning the preservation of ecclesiastical liberty. (May.) 1160

LXV.—To our dearest son in Christ, Kalojan, illustrious king of the Bulgarians.—That he shall make peace and a truce with the emperor of Constantinople and the Latins. (8 Kalends of June.) 1162

LXVI.—To the noblewoman …, countess of Blois.—The words of a certain privilege of the canons of Chartres are explained. (8 Kalends of June.) 1163

LXVII.—To the archbishop and dean of Sens.—A rescript is issued in favour of the count of Blois. (4 Kalends of June.) 1163

LXVIII.—To the bishop of Cosenza and the abbot of Cîteaux, legates of the Apostolic See.—The cause of the archbishop of Narbonne, accused of certain crimes, is entrusted to them. 1164

LXIX.—To the nobleman Raymond, count of Toulouse: may he receive a spirit of sounder counsel.—That he shall cease persecuting the Church of God. (4 Kalends of June.) 1166

LXX.—To the abbot and convent of Grand-Selve.—That they shall freely permit Hugh Vitalis, in priestly orders, to celebrate. 1168

LXXI.—To the archbishop of Tours and the bishop of Paris.—Concerning the regalia of Auxerre. (15 Kalends of June.) 1169

LXXII.—To the bishop of Treviso and Albert, priest of Mantua.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Trent. (9 Kalends of June.) 1171

LXXIII.—To the bishop of Wác.—He replies to his inquiries. (5 Ides of June.) 1173

LXXIV.—To the archbishop of Tours and his suffragans.—Concerning tournaments and aid for the Holy Land. (7 Kalends of July.) 1174

LXXV.—To the archbishop of Compostela.—That he may reconcile the altar of Saint James. (12 Kalends of July.) 1175

LXXVI.—To the same.—Concerning procurations. (10 Kalends of July.) 1175

LXXVII.—To the abbot of Saint Aubert, and Masters R. de Bekerel and R. Torel, canons of Cambrai.—Concerning a cleric who had become a monk through illness. (6 Nones of July.) 1175

LXXVIII.—To archbishops and bishops established throughout Spain and Gascony.—Concerning counterfeit insignia of Blessed James. (13 Kalends of July.) 1176

LXXIX.—To all archbishops established in Aquitaine.—Concerning apostolic letters fraudulently obtained. (5 Kalends of July.) 1176

LXXX.—To the bishop of Troyes and A., archdeacon of Paris.—That they shall restore Abbot M. to the custody of the Church of Péronne. (12 Kalends of July.) 1178

LXXXI.—To the bishop of Rochester.—That he shall compel John, deprived of office and benefice, to live with his wife. (5 Kalends of July.) 1179

LXXXII.—To the bishop of Angoulême.—Concerning canons to be promoted to the priesthood. 1180

LXXXIII.—To the bishop of Reggio and the abbot of Boscaudo.—Concerning the cause of the bishop of Nice. 1180

LXXXIV.—To the bishop and chapter of Elne.—That the opposition of one person shall not prevail against the public good. (4 Nones of July.) 1181

LXXXV.—To the bishops of Clermont and Nevers.—The cause of the bishop of Le Puy against his citizens is entrusted to them. (Nones of July.) 1181

LXXXVI.—To the podestà and citizens of Florence.—They are exhorted to peace and concord. (5 Ides of July.) 1182

LXXXVII.—To the prior and convent of Kirkham.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. 1183

LXXXVIII.—To the abbot and convent of Tulle.—Concerning the number of riding-allowances in visitations. (11 Nones of July.) 1184

LXXXIX.—To the bishops of Auxerre and Troyes, and the abbot of Saint-Bénigne.—An inquiry against the abbot and monks of Vézelay is entrusted to them. (14 Kalends of August.) 1185

XC.—To the same.—Concerning the deposition of Gilbert, abbot of Flavigny. 1187

XCI.—To the archdeacon and chapter of Venafro.—Certain rights and sentences pronounced in their favour are confirmed. (6 Kalends of August.) 1187

XCII.—To R., priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, abbot of Monte Cassino.—Certain cases of usury are entrusted to him for hearing. (9 Kalends of August.) 1190

XCIII.—To the dean and chapter of Saint Aignan of Orléans.—They are fortified by a privilege against letters of the Apostolic See. (15 Kalends of August.) 1190

XCIV.—To the abbots of Saint-Germain-des-Prés and Saint Geneviève, and to the prior of Saint Geneviève of Paris.—That they shall render full justice concerning wrongdoers against the church of Saint Aignan. 1191

XCV.—To W., dean of the church of Saint Aignan of Orléans, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (12 Kalends of August.) 1191

XCVI.—To the bishop of Meaux.—Concerning the subjection of the monastery of Rebais. (17 Kalends of July.) 1194

XCVII.—To the prior and convent of the monastery of Saint Saviour and Saint Rotrude, situated in the parish of Thérouanne.—Concerning the election of an abbot. (5 Nones of July.) 1196

XCVIII.—To Wibert, priest.—The institution of a canonry and prebend of Saint Sophia, made to him by a legate, is confirmed. (4 Kalends of August.) 1196

XCIX.—To the same.—The grant to him, made by a legate, of the provostship of Saint Anastasia is confirmed. 1197

C.—To the archbishop, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, and the archdeacon of Milan.—That they shall grant to …, a priest, leave to return to his church of Saint Michael of Vercelli. (4 Nones of August.) 1197

CI.—To the podestà and people of Florence.—They are urged to acquiesce in the admonitions of the Apostolic See and of its legate. (2 Nones of August.) 1198

CII.—To the abbess and convent of Saint Cyriacus in Gerondod.—They are absolved from payment of an annual rent of one mark of silver. (4 Nones of August.) 1199

CIII.—To R., abbot of Monte Cassino.—He says that he does not wish to answer his letters. (5 Ides of August.) 1199

CIV.—To the consuls and people of Viterbo.—That they shall not allow the girl of Amalfi to be troubled by anyone concerning her legitimacy. (3 Nones of August.) 1200

CV.—To the consuls of Viterbo. (2 Ides of August.) 1200

CVI.—To Adell., abbess of Saint Mary, Mother of God and ever-Virgin, Saint Peter, prince of the Apostles, and Saint Cyriacus the martyr, at Gerondod, and to her sisters canonically appointed.—Their liberties and immunities are confirmed, and certain privileges are granted them. (5 Ides of August.) 1200

CVII.—To the abbot of Mauléon.—He is commanded to compel A. de Scobol to return to his first wife. (14 Kalends of September.) 1203

CVIII.—To the abbot and monks of Rebais.—Their privileges and all their liberties and immunities are confirmed. (17 Kalends of September.) 1203

CIX.—To all archbishops and bishops established throughout Saxony.—Concerning the privileges of the monastery at Gerondod. (8 Kalends of September.) 1205

CX.—To the bishop of Saragossa.—It is declared what is meant by the term *novalia*, “newly cultivated land.” (11 Kalends of September.) 1205

CXI.—To the abbot of Cîteaux and Peter of Castelnau, legates of the Apostolic See.—To whom the lordship of the city of Marseilles belongs. (12 Kalends of September.) 1206

CXII.—To the archbishop of Cosenza and the bishop of Martirano.—Concerning the protection of the bishop of Mileto against Count Amfusum. (8 Kalends of September.) 1207

CXIII.—To the bishops of London, Ely, and Worcester.—Concerning the cause of the archbishop of Canterbury against the king of England. 1208

CXIV.—To the archbishop of Genoa.—A cause of divorce on account of adultery committed is entrusted to him. (Kalends of September.) 1210

CXV.—To the chapter of the Church of Ravenna.—That they shall provide their archbishop with certain pontifical vestments. 1211

CXVI.—To the archbishop of Ravenna.—Concerning the controversy between the Church of Ravenna and the commune of Faenza. (Kalends of September.) 1212

CXVII.—To the podestà and people of Pisa.—A reply is made to them concerning certain questions. (4 Ides of September.) 1215

CXVIII.—To the abbots of Decihan and Montisgerold, and the provost of Rhotnac, in the diocese of Cambrai.—That they may dispense G., a layman, and D., a woman, his wife, who are related in the fourth degree of consanguinity. (15 Kalends of September.) 1216

CXIX.—To the noblewoman Juliana, lady of Pirucis.—The things granted to her by the emperor of Constantinople are confirmed. (15 Kalends of October.) 1216

CXX.—To Henry, illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—He is granted that he may not be excommunicated except for an enormous offence. (2 Ides of September.) 1216

CXXI.—To the master of the houses of the military Order of the Temple on this side of the sea.—Concerning observance of the interdict and honouring the legate of the Apostolic See. (Ides of September.) 1217

CXXII.—To John, illustrious king of the English.—That he shall send a procurator to the Apostolic See. (3 Nones of September.) 1218

CXXIII.—To the woman Alterocca and Montanello, her son.—The sentence pronounced for them by a legate of the Apostolic See is confirmed. (2 Ides of September.) 1219

CXXIV.—To the bishop of Otten.—That a priest who has lost a finger of his left hand may minister. (14 Kalends of October.) 1221

CXXV.—To the archbishop of Varis, the bishop of Salembria, and the dean of Saint Mary of Blachernae at Constantinople.—That they shall institute R., a cleric, in the church of Kufan. (15 Kalends of October.) 1222

CXXVI.—To the bishop of Moray.—The cause of the monastery of Melrose is entrusted to him. 1222

CXXVII.—To the nobleman Maio, count of the islands of Cephalonia and Zakynthos.—He is granted leave to choose a confessor. (17 Kalends of October.) 1224

CXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Patras.—He writes to him that he should bring the bishop of Cephalonia back to obedience to the Apostolic See. (14 Kalends of October.) 1225

CXXIX.—To the bishop of Piacenza.—That he shall compel the monastery of Patramarina to restore certain goods. (18 Kalends of October.) 1226

CXXX.—To all our faithful established throughout the patrimony of Blessed Peter the Apostle.—How the Paterines and their supporters are to be punished. (9 Kalends of October.) 1226

CXXXI.—To all clerics and laymen established in the patrimony of Blessed Peter the Apostle.—That nothing be attempted contrary to laws and canons. 1227

CXXXII.—To all our faithful established throughout the patrimony of Blessed Peter the Apostle.—They are exhorted to peace and concord, and that no one injure another. 1228

CXXXIII.—To the bishops of Nevers and Orléans, and the abbot of the Court of God, of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Orléans.—Concerning Alberic, archbishop-elect of Reims. (Kalends of October.) 1228

CXXXIV.—To the same.—That the pallium be delivered to that same Alberic. 1230

CXXXV.—To the bishop of Ferns.—Concerning clerics ordained by bishops other than their own. (4 Nones of October.) 1230

CXXXVI.—To the bishop of Terdona.—A dispensation to contract marriage in the second and third degrees, for the sake of peace. (Kalends of October.) 1231

CXXXVII.—To archbishops, bishops, abbots, and others, both clerics and laymen, established throughout the kingdom of Hungary.—That they shall honourably receive the legate of the Apostolic See. (Nones of October.) 1231

CXXXVIII.—To archbishops, bishops, and all clerics and laymen established throughout Ruthenia.—That they shall treat the legate of the Apostolic See honourably. 1232

CXXXIX.—To the clergy and people of Viterbo.—That the church of Viterbo shall henceforth be a cathedral. (4 Ides of October.) 1234

CXL.—To the chapter of Uzès.—The church of Balneolis is adjudged to Peter Marco. (8 Kalends of November.) 1234

## Book Eleven

In the eleventh year of the pontificate, A.D. 1208.

I.—To the nobleman Leopold, duke of Austria.—Concerning aid for the Holy Land. (6 Kalends of March.) 1339

II.—To the same.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. 1341

V. 1343
