April.) 1362 XXXVI.—To the dean, cantor, and treasurer of Saint Sophia at Constantinople.—A certain case against the Templars is entrusted to them. 1363 XXXVII.—To the deans of Saint Paul, Saint Michael of Bucca Leonis, and Saint Anastasia at Constantinople.—Written to them on behalf of Master W. Cocart. (Sixth day before the Kalends of April.) 1363 XXXVIII.—To his dearest son in Christ, the illustrious emperor of Constantinople.—Concerning the oath of fidelity which prelates owe the emperor. (Sixth day before the Ides of May.) 1429 CXII.—To the archbishop and chapter of Athens.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Sixth day before the Ides of July.) 1432 CXIII.—To the archbishop and chapter of Athens.—That the Church of Athens be ordered according to the customs of the Church of Paris. (Second day before the Ides of July.) 1433 CXIV.—To the bishop of Demetrias.—The bishopric of Calydon is entrusted to him. 1433 CXV.—To the bishop-elect of Citrum.—The bishopric of Platamon is entrusted to him. 1433 CXVI.—To the noblemen, lords of Thebes.—That they pay tithes to the Church of Thebes. 1434 CXVII.—To the noblemen, lords of Negroponte.—Concerning the same matter. 1434 CXVIII.—To the noblemen, lords of Thermopylae, and the lords of Thebes.—Concerning the same matter. 1434 CXIX.—To the nobleman Roland Pissa.—Concerning the same matter. 1434 CXX.—To the nobleman, constable of Thessalonica.—That he restore the dignities and possessions of the Church of Demetrias. 1434 CXXI.—To the nobleman O. de la Roche, duke of Athens.—Concerning the payment of tithes. 1435 CXXII.—To the archbishop of Larissa.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Sixth day before the Ides of July.) 1435 CXXIII.—To the master and brethren of the Hospital of Saint Samson at Constantinople.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. 1435 CXXIV.—To the abbot and convent of Fossanova.—Concerning the dedication of an altar. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of August.) 1435 CXXV.—To Raynald, archbishop of Capua, and his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Tenth day before the Kalends of August.) 1437 CXXVI.—To Raynald, archbishop of Capua.—A sentence pronounced by Alexander III is confirmed. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of August [printed: *Augustini*].) 1439 CXXVII.—To the prior and clergy of Saints John and Paul of Todi.—The church of Saint Hilary is adjudged to them. 1442 CXXVIII.—To our nephew Stephen.—A prebend at Bayeux is adjudged to him. (Nones of July.) 1443 CXXIX.—To the beloved sons, Major and William, archdeacons, and the prior of Saint Victor of Paris.—Concerning the prebend of Saint Martin of Tours adjudged to Master William. (Eighth day before the Ides of August.) 1445 CXXX.—To the counts, barons, citizens, and other faithful of the realm established in Apulia.—Concerning assistance to be given to the king of Sicily. 1447 CXXXI.—To Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Theodore, legate of the Apostolic See, and O., our acolyte.—Concerning the same matter. 1448 CXXXII. 1448 CXXXIII.—To the counts, barons, citizens, and other faithful of the realm established from Salerno to Ceprano, from sea to sea.—Concerning the same matter. 1449 CXXXIV.—To the illustrious king of Aragon.—Concerning the marriage of Frederick, king of Sicily. (Sixth day before the Ides of August.) 1449 CXXXV.—To the noblemen, rectors, consuls, castellans, citizens, and other faithful of ours established throughout Campania.—Concerning the coinage to be accepted throughout all Campania. (Nones of August.) 1449 CXXXVI.—To the bishop of Aversa.—A mandate concerning the first prebend to fall vacant. (Eighth day before the Kalends of August.) 1450 CXXXVII.—To the abbot and clergy of Saint Mary of the River of Ceccano.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Fourteenth day before the Kalends of September.) 1450 CXXXVIII.—To the bishop of Troyes.—Written against the canons of Saint Martin of Troyes. (Seventeenth day before the Kalends of September.) 1451 CXXXIX.—To John of Carbone and Benedict, brothers.—An exchange made between them and the monastery of Monte Cassino is confirmed. (Second day before the Ides of August.) 1453 CXL.—To the master of the Order of Saint James.—He replies to his questions. (Kalends of September.) 1454 CXLI.—To the bishops of London, Ely, and Worcester.—Concerning the case of the Church of Canterbury. (Eleventh day before the Kalends of September.) 1455 CXLII.—To the bishop of Meaux and the archdeacon of Paris.—That notorious and criminal persons not possess prebends in the Church of Chartres. (Seventeenth day before the Kalends of October.) 1457 CXLIII.—To the bishop and clergy of Narni.—That they observe the interdict imposed upon the city. 1458 CXLIV.—To the abbots of Vendôme in the diocese of Chartres and of Saint Julian of Tours, and the prior of the greater monastery of Tours.—Concerning reform of the monastery of Bourgueil. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of October.) 1459 CXLV.—To Luke, abbot of the monastery of Bourgueil, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Eleventh day before the Kalends of October.) 1460 CXLVI.—To the rectors of the Roman confraternity.—A reply to their questions. (Tenth day before the Kalends of October.) 1463 CXLVII.—To the rector and brethren of the Hospital of Saint Bartholomew in Silice at Lucca.—The question concerning the election of the rector of that hospital is decided. (Fourth day before the Nones of August.) 1464 CXLVIII.—To the abbot and convent of Coldriz, of the Premonstratensian Order.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Seventh day before the Kalends of September.) 1465 CXLIX.—To the chapter of Tours. (Fourth day before the Nones of October.) 1465 CL.—The following letter lacks an address in the old codex.—Concerning the election of the abbess of Mantignano. 1466 CLI.—To Bartholomew, bishop of Cardica.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Third day before the Nones of October.) 1466 CLII.—To the archbishops of Patras and Thebes, and the bishop of Thermopylae.—That they admonish the lady of Thessalonica concerning her duty. (Fourth day before the Nones of October.) 1467 CLIII.—To the archbishops of Larissa and Athens, and the bishop of Sithonia.—Concerning tithes and first-fruits of the Church of Thebes. (Sixth day before the Ides of October.) 1468 CLIV.—To the archbishops of Athens and Thebes, and the bishop of Castoria.—Written on behalf of the clergy of Larissa. (Fourth day before the Nones of October.) 1468 CLV.—To the archbishop of Larissa.—That he observe the Latin rite in consecrations. (Fourth day before the Nones of October.) 1468 CLVI.—To the archbishops and bishops, and the beloved sons the abbots, priors, and other prelates of churches established throughout the kingdom of France.—Crusaders are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Fifth day before the Ides of October.) 1469 CLVII.—To all clerics signed for, or to be signed for, Christ’s service against the heretics of Provence.—Concerning the same matter. (Eighth day before the Ides of October.) 1469 CLVIII.—To the archbishops and bishops and the beloved sons, other prelates of churches established in the kingdom of France.—Concerning the same matter. (Seventh day before the Ides of October.) 1469 CLIX.—To Philip, illustrious king of the French.—That Jews remit interest to crusaders. (Seventh day before the Ides of October.) 1470 CLX.—To the archbishop of Larissa.—Permission is given him to reside at Ferchika. (Third day before the Ides of October.) 1471 CLXI.—To Master Aimer, canon of Saint Andrew of Poitiers.—A reply to his questions. (Fifteenth day before the Kalends of November.) 1471 CLXII.—To William Doiard, canon of Thebes.—His prebend at Thebes is confirmed. (Thirteenth day before the Kalends of November.) 1472 CLXIII.—To Walter, bishop of Catania, chancellor of the kingdom of Sicily.—That he show reverence and honour to the archbishop of Monreale. (Thirteenth day before the Kalends of November.) 1472 CLXIV.—To Bartholomew of Ceprano.—A certain sentence pronounced in his favour is confirmed. (Tenth day before the Kalends of September.) 1473 CLXV.—To the archbishop of Milan, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—Concerning whether fiefs may be alienated. (Tenth day before the Kalends of November.) 1474 CLXVI.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Vincent.—Tithes are adjudged to them. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of November.) 1474 CLXVII.—To the bishop of Lucca.—The privileges of the monastery of Fichecho are confirmed. (Second day before the Kalends of November.) 1475 CLXVIII.—To the abbot and monks of Saint Saviour of Fichecho.—Concerning the same matter. 1477 CLXIX.—To Gerard, founder of the chapel established in the suburb of Vienne in honour of the Holy Spirit and Blessed Anthony.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Eleventh day before the Kalends of November.) 1477 CLXX.—To the archbishop of Benevento.—Concerning the gift of a certain church. 1478 CLXXI.—To the archbishops of Larissa and Thebes.—That they inquire concerning the candidate for the Church of Thessalonica. (Kalends of November.) 1478 CLXXII.—To the beloved son Pons, abbot of the monastery of Saint Giles, and his successors regularly appointed, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Second day before the Ides of November.) 1480 CLXXIII.—To the archbishop of London.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Sleswick. (Second day before the Nones of November.) 1483 CLXXIV.—To the bishops of Växjö, Linköping, and Skara.—That they restrain Eric, invader of the kingdom of Sweden. (Ides of November.) 1485 CLXXV.—To the archbishop of Milan, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, the bishop of Ypres, and the beloved son the abbot of Tilleto.—Against the city of Piacenza. (Tenth day before the Kalends of December.) 1486 CLXXVI.—To the bishop of Bayeux.—A reply to his questions. (Tenth day before the Kalends of December.) 1489 CLXXVII.—To the bishop of Florence, the abbot of Saxivivo, and the Camaldolese prior.—The visitation of the monasteries of Tuscany is entrusted to them. (Seventh day before the Kalends of December.) 1490 CLXXVIII.—To the archbishops of Tarragona, Braga, and Compostela.—That brethren of Saint John of Jerusalem may not transfer to the Cistercians. (Sixth day before the Kalends of December.) 1491 CLXXIX.—To the archbishop of Neopatras, the bishop of Davalia, and the abbot of Saint Luke in the diocese of Negroponte.—Written on behalf of Theodore, bishop of Negroponte. (Sixth day before the Ides of December.) 1492.

[Col. 1664] CLXXX.—Letter of Philip, king of the French, to the lord pope.—Concerning the divorce case. 1493 CLXXXI.—To his dearest son in Christ, Philip, illustrious king of the French.—Reply to the preceding letter. (Seventh day before the Ides of December.) 1493 CLXXXII.—To the same.—Concerning the same matter. (Fifth day before the Ides of December.) 1494 CLXXXIII.—To the beloved son Guala, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the same matter. 1499 CLXXXIV.—To the archbishops of Mainz and Magdeburg.—Concerning the marriage of the king of Bohemia. (Third day before the Ides of December.) 1499 CLXXXV.—To all Christ’s faithful established throughout Lombardy and the March.—Concerning aid for the Holy Land. (Fourth day before the Ides of December.) 1500 CLXXXVI.—To the archbishops and bishops and other prelates of churches established throughout Lombardy and the March.—Concerning the same matter. 1503 CLXXXVII.—To the bishop of Ypres and the abbot of Tilleto, visitors of Lombardy.—Concerning the removal of the bishop of Albi. (Second day before the Ides of December.) 1503 CLXXXVIII.—To the prior of Oseney and the superior of Saint Frideswide’s.—Written on behalf of the abbot of Bello. (Second day before the Ides of December.) 1504 CLXXXIX.—To the archbishop of Neopatras, the bishop of Davalia, and the beloved son, bishop-elect of Nazores.—Concerning the obedience which bishops owe their metropolitans. (Sixth day before the Ides of December.) 1505 CXC.—To the bishop-elect of Nazores.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Fifth day before the Ides of December.) 1506 CXCI.—To the bishop of Davalia.—Concerning the same subject. 1506 CXCII.—To the bishop and archdeacon of Cremona.—Concerning the election of the abbot of Cornu. (Sixteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1506 CXCIII.—To Sigibald, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Rosevelde, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Fifth day before the Ides of December.) 1507 CXCIV.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Vaast of Arras.—Concerning the liberty of that monastery. (Sixteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1509 CXCV.—To the prior and brethren of Andres.—That they may recover possessions which have been pledged. (Thirteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1509 CXCVI.—To the archbishop and suffragans of the Church of Tarragona.—Concerning the case of Durand of Huesca and his companions. (Fifteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1510 CXCVII.—To Durand of Huesca and his brethren, called the Poor Catholics, remaining in the Catholic faith.—Concerning the same matter. 1514 CXCVIII.—To Durand of Huesca and his brethren remaining in the Catholic faith.—That they are not bound to go to war against Christians. (Fifteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1514 CXCIX.—To the prior and brethren of the monastery of Andres.—Concerning the construction of no chapels within the bounds of the monastery. (Sixteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1514 CC.—To Henry, prior of the monastery of Andres, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of January.) 1515 CCI.—To the abbot and convent of Karoff.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Thirteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1517 CCII.—To the bishop, archdeacon, and chapter of Thérouanne.—That they exact nothing from the abbot of Andres for benediction. (Tenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1517 CCIII.—To the bishop and chapter of Châlons.—That they admit Walter to a prebend. (Thirteenth day before the Kalends of January.) 1517 CCIV.—To the abbots of Longpont and Igny, and the prior of Igny in the diocese of Soissons.—That R., a subdeacon, return to his wife. (Third day before the Kalends of January.) 1518 CCV.—To the dean of Salisbury residing at Paris, A., archdeacon, and Master P. Peverel, canon of Paris.—Concerning the election of the abbot of Andres. (Third day before the Nones of January.) 1519 CCVI.—To the bishop of Włocławek [*Wlterrano*, uncertain].—A certain matrimonial case is entrusted to him. (Third day before the Ides of January.) 1521 CCVII.—Letter of Henry, emperor of Constantinople, to the lord pope.—Concerning the defeat of Voullae at Philippopolis. (September.) 1522 CCVIII.—To his dearest son in Christ, Frederick, illustrious king of Sicily.—He is urged not to claim spiritual jurisdiction for himself. (Fifth day before the Ides of January.) 1523 CCIX.—To the prior of Saint Thomas the Martyr of Acre and of Saint George of Sisto, and his brethren.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Fourth day before the Ides of January.) 1523 CCX.—To the prior and brethren of Tinemvahe.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Third day before the Nones of January.) 1526 CCXI.—To the bishops of London, Ely, and Worcester.—Concerning the affair of Canterbury. (Second day before the Ides of January.) 1526 CCXII.—To the prior and convent of Coventry.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Coventry. (Ides of January.) 1528 CCXIII.—Concerning the same subject. 1529 CCXIV.—To the bishops of London, Ely, and Worcester.—Concerning permission to celebrate during an interdict. 1529 CCXV.—To the same.—That communion is not to be held with the excommunicated. (Second day before the Ides of January.) 1530 CCXVI.—To Stephen, archbishop of Canterbury, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church.—Concerning the same matter. 1530 CCXVII.—To the same.—Concerning permission to celebrate during an interdict. 1531 CCXVIII.—To the bishop of Winchester.—That he carry out the things which the above-named bishops have enjoined upon him. (Ides of January.) 1531 CCXIX.—To Hervey, bishop of Troyes, and his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Fifteenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1531 CCXX.—To the illustrious king of Hungary.—Concerning the affair of the bishop of Bamberg and the archbishop of Kalocsa. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of February.) 1534 CCXXI.—To the illustrious king of England.—Concerning the affair of Canterbury. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1535 CCXXII.—To Gerard, treasurer of the Church of Thebes.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Sixth day before the Kalends of September.) 1537 CCXXIII.—To John, illustrious king of the English.—That he restore the goods of B., queen of the English. (Twelfth day before the Kalends of February.) 1537 CCXXIV.—To the bishops of Rochester and Salisbury.—Concerning the same matter. 1539 CCXXV.—To the provost and chapter of Brioude.—Concerning their exemption. (Fifth day before the Kalends of February.) 1540 CCXXVI.—To the abbot of Saint Geneviève, the archdeacon, and Master P. Peverel, canon of Paris.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Thérouanne. (Fourth day before the Kalends of February.) 1542 CCXXVII.—To the same persons.—Concerning the same matter. (Third day before the Kalends of February.) 1544 CCXXVIII.—To the bishop of Le Puy and the abbots of Saint Peter and of Sécuré.—The case of the canons of Brioude is entrusted to them. (Fifth day before the Kalends of February.) 1544 CCXXIX.—To the illustrious king of France.—He is urged to attack the heretics of Provence. (Third day before the Nones of February.) 1545 CCXXX.—To all the faithful who will contend in Christ’s service against the heretics of Provence.—Concerning the same subject. 1545 CCXXXI.—To all the faithful signed for, or to be signed for, Christ’s service against the heretics of Provence, established both within and outside the kingdom of France.—They are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. 1546 CCXXXII.—To the bishops of Riez and Couserans, and the abbot of Cîteaux, legates of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the affair of the county of Melgueil. 1546 CCXXXIII.—To the same.—Concerning the affair of the faith. 1547 CCXXXIV.—To the same.—That they absolve Guy, count of Auvergne. 1547 CCXXXV.—To the abbot of Cîteaux, legate of the Apostolic See.—He is reproved for improper suspicions. 1547 CCXXXVI.—To the archbishop of Bordeaux.—Concerning the grant of a prebend at Saintes to Fulch. (Nones of February.) 1548 CCXXXVII.—To the abbot of Saint Aubert, the dean, and Master R. de Bekerel, canon of Cambrai.—That they admit Giles to the priesthood. 1549 CCXXXVIII.—To the archbishop of Athens.—He is received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1549 CCXXXIX.—To Hugh, canon of Thebes.—The church of Kalenda is confirmed to him. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1549 CCXL.—To Robert of Sucy, canon of Athens.—His prebend at Athens is confirmed. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1550 CCXLI.—To Master William, canon of Thebes.—Concerning the same subject. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1550 CCXLII.—To Hugh, canon of Thebes.—Concerning the same subject. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1550 CCXLIII.—To Master Ranulf, dean of Davalia.—His deanery in the Church of Davalia is confirmed. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1550 CCXLIV.—To the archbishop of Larissa and the beloved sons, bishops-elect of Citrum and Nazores.—Written to them on behalf of the archbishop of Athens. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1550 CCXLV.—To the noblemen Balmo, constable of Thessalonica; Otto de la Roche, lord of Athens; . . . marquis; . . . lord of Negroponte; T. de Ostremuncout; and the other princes of Romania.—Concerning the payment of tithes. (Ninth day before the Kalends of February.) 1551 CCXLVI.—To the archbishop of Athens.—Concerning the residence of canons.

[Col. 1666] 1551 CCXLVII.—To the bishop-elect of Nazores.—Concerning the same matter. (Eighth day before the Kalends of February.) 1552 CCXLVIII.—To the bishop of Ely.—Concerning the precentor of the Church of London. (Second day before the Nones of February.) 1552 CCXLIX.—To Hubald, bishop elected archbishop of Ravenna.—That he procure the election of a bishop for the Church of Faenza. (Fourth day before the Ides of February.) 1553 CCL.—To the abbot and canons of the Lord’s Temple.—They are received under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Eleventh day before the Kalends of February.) 1555 CCLI.—To the abbot and convent of Molesme.—Concerning visitation of the monastery of Molesme. (Sixth day before the Ides of February.) 1555 CCLII.—To the archbishop of Larissa, the bishop of Davalia, and the bishop-elect of Citrum.—Concerning the residence of canons in a safe place. (Eighth day before the Ides of February.) 1557 CCLIII.—To the abbot and convent of Saint Maurus of Angers.—The church of Saint Peter of Cultures is adjudged to them. (Third day before the Ides of February.) 1557 CCLIV.—To the bishop and chapter of Lisieux.—Concerning the treasury and prebend at Lisieux reserved by the pope. (Second day before the Ides of February.) 1558 CCLV.—To the bishop of Arras and the abbots of Dunes and of Ourscamp, of the dioceses of Thérouanne and Noyon.—Concerning the granting of prebends at Aire. (Fourteenth day before the Kalends of March.) 1559 CCLVI.—To Berard, archbishop of Athens, and his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Ides of February.) 1559 CCLVII.—To the bishop of Paris.—Concerning a forger-cleric. (Fourteenth day before the Kalends of March.) 1562 CCLVIII.—To the bishop of Avranches.—Concerning the right of patronage. (Second day before the Ides of February.) 1563 CCLIX.—To all bishops established throughout England.—A commission against those who did not observe the interdict. (Ninth day before the Kalends of March.) 1563 CCLX.—To the abbot of Cîteaux, legate of the Apostolic See.—Concerning the same matter. (Ninth day before the Kalends of March.) 1564 CCLXI.—To the bishop-elect of Meaux, the abbot of Saint Geneviève, and William, archdeacon of Paris.—Concerning the election of the bishop of Verdun. (Tenth day before the Kalends of March.) 1566 CCLXII.—To Cynthius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, legate of the Apostolic See.—He replies to his questions. 1567 CCLXIII.—To the archbishop and Master Gernand, canon of Magdeburg.—Concerning the election of the abbess of Heris. 1570 CCLXIV.—To the archbishop of Tours and the abbots of Marmoutier and Saint Julian of Tours.—A case concerning the *succentoria* of Poitiers is entrusted to them. 1575 CCLXV.—To the bishops of Paris and Troyes, and the abbot of Saint Geneviève of Paris.—Concerning the case of the monastery of Vézelay against the count of Auxerre. 1576 CCLXVI.—How witnesses are to be received. 1582 CCLXVII.—To the bishop of Ferrara.—A reply to his questions. 1582 CCLXVIII.—To the bishop of Saint Andrews, the abbot of Berborc, T., prior, R., archdeacon, and Master L., official of Saint Andrews. 1583 CCLXIX.—He replies to someone’s consultation. 1583 CCLXX.—To the bishops of Florence and Fiesole, and the archpriest of Pistoia.—The hospital of Saint Allucius is adjudged to the Hospitallers. 1583 CCLXXI.—To the bishop of Poitiers.—He replies to his questions. 1584 CCLXXII.—To the bishop of Auxerre. 1585 CCLXXIII.—To Leo, cardinal-priest of the title of Holy Cross.—Concerning the ordination of the abbot of Saint Quiricus. 1585 CCLXXIV.—To all doctors of Sacred Scripture, decrees, and liberal arts residing at Paris.—A certain statute of theirs is confirmed. 1585 CCLXXV.—Apostolic letters are not valid beyond one year. 1587 CCLXXVI.—To the abbots of Saint Mary in Cagia and of the Secret Valley, and M., canon of Reims.—An accusation against the abbot of Saint Denis of Reims is entrusted to them. 1587 CCLXXVII.—To the chapter of Messina.—Permission is granted to him to cohabit with the second wife whom he married while the first was living. 1589.

**APPENDIX TO BOOK ELEVEN**

CCLXXVIII.—To the beloved sons, the brethren of the monastery of Saint Prosper situated below the city of Reggio, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Tenth day before the Kalends of February.) 1589 CCLXXIX.—To the chapter of Bivins.—Concerning confirmation of privileges. (Third day before the Nones of February.) 1591 CCLXXX.—To Hubald, bishop of Faenza.—He is transferred to the Church of Ravenna. 1592.

[Col. 1667] CCLXXXI.—To Roffrid, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, and to the abbot and convent of Monte Cassino.—Concerning revocation of alienations. (Eighth day before the Kalends of August.) 1593 CCLXXXII.—To the beloved sons Roffrid, abbot of the monastery of Saint Benedict of Monte Cassino, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity. 1594.

It seemed fitting to publish here also the following letters, although they were not issued in the eleventh year, because they concern the case dealt with in letter 56 of this book. For that reason we have also added the letters of Honorius II and III, and the letters of Cardinal Romanus concerning the settlement between the bishop of Meaux and the abbess of Jouarre; after these there follow again several letters of Innocent III and Alexander III on the same subject.

I.—To the bishop of Paris and the abbot of Lagny.—Against the abbess of Jouarre. 1599 II.—To the same persons. 1599 III.—To the beloved sons, the abbots of Longpont in the diocese of Soissons and of Saint-Just in the diocese of Beauvais, and Master G., archdeacon of Soissons. (Eleventh day before the Kalends of January.) 1600 IV.—To the beloved sons, the dean of Saint Thomas of Crépy in the diocese of Senlis, Germend, canon of Soissons, and Master Gerard of Saint Denis, canon of Noyon. 1603 V.—To the beloved sons, the abbots of Saint-Just in the diocese of Beauvais and of Longpont, and G., archdeacon of Soissons. 1604 VI.—Letter of Honorius III concerning the same controversy. 1605 VII.—Settlement made between the bishop of Mende and the Church of Jouarre. 1606 VIII.—Letter of Innocent III to the bishop-elect of Catalonia and the abbot of Trois-Fontaines, mentioned above in letter 2, to the bishop of Paris and the abbot of Lagny. 1611 IX.—Letter of Honorius II concerning the subjection of the monasteries of Rebais and Jouarre. 1611 X.—Letter of Alexander III by which he confirms the foregoing letters of Honorius II. 1612
[Col. 1667] END OF THE TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTEENTH VOLUME.
